tasks.title: Choose and rehearse the production cutover
tasks.why: The domain still uses the beta backend. A URL/key swap can strand business data, storage, tokens and callbacks.

tasks.why: The runtime API identifies Hobby retention; Hobby is not a commercial launch plan. Supabase compute/backups/provider quotas also need verification.

tasks.title: Release ordinary customer onboarding safely
tasks.why: The ten-tester grant, tier testing and approved-recipient rules cannot be the production entitlement model.

tasks.why: Some browser/financial fixtures predate the PDF handoff and current labels; the domain-bound branch auto-deploys before a complete test certificate.
tasks.acceptance: Update obsolete fixtures without weakening functional assertions; pass complete current build, financial/tenant/voice/storage/calendar and authenticated browser journeys for the same immutable release commit. Enforce required checks and staged deployment/promotion before domain release; unify supported Node versions and include the actual release branch in CI.

tasks.title: Harden Auth and privileged accounts
tasks.why: Leaked-password protection and bounded sessions are now enabled; production authentication delivery, infrastructure MFA, emergency recovery and measured abuse resistance still need certification.

tasks.title: Finish independent tenant, RPC and storage security review
tasks.why: RLS presence and zero ERROR lints do not prove correct policies; public definer/token endpoints intentionally bypass normal login.
tasks.acceptance: Review all anon/authenticated definer grants and fixed search paths, operator functions, AI/tool authorization, customer token expiry/revocation, storage isolation, webhook signatures/replay and CSP. Test at least two real tenant sessions across role changes and expired sessions; clear exploitable high findings and record intentional exceptions. Never add permissive policies to internal deny-by-default tables.

tasks.title: Add distributed abuse limits and backpressure
tasks.why: Monthly quotas, one calendar OAuth limiter and client buttons are not complete per-minute abuse protection.
tasks.acceptance: Enforce account/business/IP burst limits on public token reads, signup, AI/voice, PDF, OCR, uploads and sends; verify retry-after behavior, concurrent quota races, upload/content bounds and global provider-cost ceilings. Use a shared store or atomic database counters, not per-instance memory alone.

tasks.title: Prove backup and recovery
tasks.why: No current restore drill or storage recovery evidence establishes a safe recovery point.
tasks.acceptance: Confirm database backups/PITR as selected, separately back up private storage objects and configuration, restore an isolated full business and verify document/file hashes, permissions and financial totals. Measure recovery time/data loss against approved RTO/RPO; protect backup credentials and rehearse rollback.

tasks.title: Install operational monitoring and route alerts
tasks.why: PostHog is product analytics, not an error or uptime monitor; limited/empty runtime logs leave major blind spots.
tasks.acceptance: Configure Sentry or equivalent error tracing, Vercel real-user Web Vitals, synthetic public/authenticated smoke monitors, provider/queue/DB dashboards and spend alerts. Scrub contact/document content, tokens, query strings and audio. Trigger a test incident and verify it reaches the named on-call owner; set retention and sampling budgets. Surface safe error, uptime and performance summaries in the Finviant Admin Dashboard with last-checked time, degraded/unavailable states and links to restricted provider dashboards. Keep raw customer content, tokens and privileged logs out of summaries. Verify a simulated outage/error reaches the owner and appears in the dashboard; current database/queue counts alone do not satisfy this gate.

tasks.title: Verify scheduled work and reconcile uncertain deliveries
tasks.why: Active cron schedules and accepted HTTP dispatches do not establish successful background work.
tasks.acceptance: Observe actual worker completion, heartbeat age, queue lag, failed/dead tasks, token refresh, provider 429s, expired leases, duplicate/missed runs and outage recovery. Provide operator review for uncertain sends; alert without automatically duplicating a possibly delivered message.

tasks.title: Tune RLS, queries and connection budgets
tasks.why: Advisors flag 23 RLS evaluation warnings and 49 missing FK indexes on a tiny database.
tasks.acceptance: Review plans on representative tenant sizes; fix applicable auth initplan patterns and high-value FK/filter/order indexes, then rerun tenant authorization tests. Verify transaction pooler/TLS/dedicated calendar role, aggregate serverless pool limits (calendar pool max=3 per instance), Auth reserve, timeouts and pagination. Measure before/after; do not blindly drop 39 unused indexes.

tasks.title: Measure capacity with realistic isolated tenant load
tasks.why: One business and a malformed-input campaign do not establish a hundreds-of-business capacity claim.
tasks.acceptance: Use isolated, provider-approved staging and synthetic distinct authenticated tenants; run smoke, 10/50/100-concurrent-user ramps across at least 300 workspaces, then a 60-minute soak and queue catch-up. Cover realistic invoices/jobs/history/photos, concurrent bookings/payments, PDF/AI/OCR work with bounded stub providers, and second-tenant isolation. Record p95/p99 latency, failures, saturation and cost; proceed toward 1,000 workspaces only after the first target passes.

tasks.title: Release general transactional email

Inbox placement cannot be guaranteed.

Paid entitlements must come from verified provider state, never user metadata or test tier selection. Match the Finviant Pricing proposal ($14.99 Individual / $28 Business), fixed payment-recovery grace and lifecycle dates; verify additional-request purchases without automatic overages.

tasks.acceptance: Verify merchant onboarding, hosted checkout/payment links, account binding, signatures/replay, deposit/partial/full payments, refunds/disputes, dashboard balance and activity. tasks.title: Set customer support, privacy and incident operations

Confirm refund/cancellation procedures before charging. Establish a connected-chat troubleshooting workflow with read-only investigation by default, explicit owner authorization for consequential writes (data deletion, billing changes and major deployments), least-privilege/revocable provider access and auditable changes. Retain direct owner access to all providers, a named backup developer and an emergency runbook. Keep assessment evidence, incident history and handoff instructions current. Verify EXPORT-01, disclosed terms, payment recovery/reactivation races, tenant isolation, multi-workspace Auth safety, legal holds, provider tokens/queues/public links and database plus actual Storage/derived/orphan file cleanup. proposals.title: Finviant Pricing
proposals.body:
This is the consolidated commercial proposal, including the new inactive-account policy. It supersedes earlier proposed prices and Fin allowances. Saving this proposal does not activate subscriptions, change current entitlements or enable record deletion. Preserve the administrator's management access and tier-testing tools, and the existing no-charge, nonexpiring Business beta grants until a separately planned migration.

### Plan options and limits

| Feature / allowance | Free | Individual | Business |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Monthly price | $0 | $14.99 | $28.00 |
| Access term | One 90-day period from explicit Free activation | While subscription is paid | While subscription is paid |
| Requests to Fin | 3 introductory requests total, shared with the trial | 25 per billing month | 100 per billing month, shared by the business |
| Estimates and invoices | Unlimited creation during the active term | Unlimited | Unlimited |
| PDFs, customer approval and payment links | Included | Included | Included |
| Verified approval/payment updates | Included in applicable records and dashboard | Included | Included |
| Active customers | 10 | Unlimited | Unlimited |
| File storage | 100 MB | 2 GB | 5 GB shared |
| Account access | 1 owner | 1 owner | 5 people including owner |
| Internal worker profiles | Owner only | 5 including owner | 25 including owner |
| Voice transcription | Not included outside the trial | 60 minutes/month | 90 minutes/month shared |
| Managed email recipient deliveries | Send through own email app | 250/month | 1,000/month shared |
| Managed SMS | Send through own text app | Send through own text app | 100 US SMS segments/month shared, after paid activation and sender verification |
| Receipt scans | Not included outside the trial | 50/month | 100/month shared |
| Customer self-booking from approved estimates | Not included | Not included | Included with availability and schedule updates |
| E-Business Card | Not included | Not included | One company card; unlimited vCard downloads and device sharing; managed delivery uses email/SMS limits |
| Document branding | Finviant branding | Business logo; remove Finviant branding | Business logo; remove Finviant branding |

Worker profiles are an internal list for assignments and availability; they do not grant sign-in access. Business account seats are separate authorized users. Counts and usage are shared per business, not multiplied by seats. Unlimited documents do not mean unlimited file storage, managed messages or Fin use. Quotas must be visible before an action; ordinary manual work and export remain usable when Fin is exhausted. Long or Unicode texts can use multiple SMS segments; show the segment count before sending.

Retain the designed paid-plan features: financial history, external calendar connections, recurring invoice drafts for owner review, worker hours/time off/assignments and QuickBooks read-only import. Free retains the proposed last-30-day reporting view during its active term. Individual email covers owner-initiated sends and basic overdue-invoice reminders; Business adds scheduled communications, broader reminders and customer scheduling. Third-party activation, processor transaction fees and SMS registration requirements must be disclosed separately. Do not advertise a live integration until its acceptance gate is verified. Preserve other existing manual features and limits unless separately revised.

### One Business trial, followed by an explicit plan choice

Offer one 15-day Business trial per business/primary owner, beginning after verified onboarding and workspace activation. No separate Individual trial, required card or automatic paid enrollment. Enable Business workflows with these total trial allowances: 3 requests to Fin, 2 transcription minutes within those requests, 25 managed email recipient deliveries, 3 receipt scans, 10 active customers and 100 MB storage. Managed SMS starts only after paid activation and required verification. Own email/text apps remain the sending fallback when a managed delivery allowance is exhausted.

Trial and Free share the same 3 introductory Fin requests; choosing Free does not grant another 3. Send trial-end reminders 3 days and 1 day before expiry. At trial end present these choices in this order:

1. Activate Business — $28/month.
2. Activate Individual — $14.99/month.
3. Activate Free — $0 for 90 days.

No selection means an expired, read-only workspace with a fixed deletion deadline; it does not start another trial or create a subscription. Free starts only when explicitly selected and is available once per business. Switching plans, signing in or restarting onboarding does not restart trial, Free or deletion clocks. Trial-created records are preserved during the retention window; lower plans disable unavailable team access and automation while retaining export access to those records. Existing trial-only SMS restrictions and sender verification remain enforced.

### Requests to Fin and additional purchases

Use the customer-facing phrase “requests to Fin,” not credits, tokens or searches. One successfully completed user task uses one request; internal provider calls, lookups, clarification steps and automatic retries do not create extra customer charges. Failed tasks release the reserved request. Manual document creation, sending, export, customer approvals, payments and resulting status changes do not consume Fin requests. Free introductory use is limited to document drafting; paid plans receive their designed assistant capabilities.

Enforce a bounded heavy-request workload and track tokens/provider costs internally. Tell the user upfront when a task exceeds supported scope instead of silently charging multiple requests. Reserve usage atomically, settle once on success and prevent duplicate charges across retries and concurrent tabs. Paid monthly included allowances reset on the billing cycle and do not roll over.

Offer paid plans explicitly purchased packs of 100 additional requests to Fin for $6.99 or 250 for $15.99, with a separate purchased balance. No automatic overage purchase. Disclose the final pack expiry/refund terms before checkout; these terms still need to be finalized. A request pack does not extend an account's subscription, Free period or record-retention deadline.

### Inactive and expired accounts — recommended retention policy

Use paid entitlement and a fixed expiry date to control storage retention. A login, background sync, email open, customer-link visit or automated payment callback must not keep an unpaid workspace in storage indefinitely.

| Account or workspace state | Access and recommended retention |
| --- | --- |
| Active paid Individual or Business | Keep records within the subscribed storage limit while payment is current. After 180 days without an owner sign-in, send a service reminder; do not delete data or cancel a paying subscription solely for inactivity. |
| Active 15-day trial or active 90-day Free period | Honor the advertised term even if the owner has not signed in. Show the exact end date and subsequent deletion date. |
| Trial ends with no plan selection | Stop creation/sending and paid automation. Allow owner view/download/export for 60 days from trial end, then delete the workspace's records. A first eligible Free activation or verified paid activation before deletion can restore entitled access. |
| Free reaches its 90-day end | Stop creation/sending and paid automation. Allow owner view/download/export for 60 days, then delete the workspace's records unless paid access is activated. No second Free period. |
| Paid subscription cancelled or not renewed | Retain normal access through the paid-through date. At entitlement end, allow 60 days of owner view/download/export, then delete unless paid access resumes or an unused eligible Free period is explicitly selected. |
| Failed subscription payment | Recommend one fixed 7-day payment-recovery grace period after failed renewal, with notices and no duplicate billing. Do not refill paid Fin or managed-delivery allowances until renewal payment is verified. If unpaid at its end, begin the same 60-day read-only retention period. Repeated retries or sign-ins cannot restart it. |
| Unverified signup or account that never activates a workspace | Remove abandoned signup/onboarding data after 30 days from signup, with notices 7 days and 1 day before deletion. Exclude any account with a paid, active, beta-exempt or other retained workspace membership. |

The 60-day window is the full owner recovery/export window; do not add an indefinite archive afterward. Use server-generated UTC deadlines, display the owner's local date/time and retain policy-version acceptance. A trial immediately followed by the 90-day Free period provides up to 105 days of active use, then 60 days to export: records are deleted on day 165 if no paid activation occurs. Ordinary backup copies must then age out within the separately disclosed backup window.

Send a clear in-app notice and transactional email when paid/free access ends, then deletion warnings 30 days, 7 days and 1 day before the scheduled purge. Each notice must state the exact date, affected business, what will be lost, the export link and the plan activation link. Do not use marketing opt-out settings to suppress necessary account-service notices. Track delivery/retries and expose failures to the administrator; a bounced email must not silently become an unlimited retention extension. Show both upcoming deletions and failed cleanup jobs in the Admin Dashboard.

During read-only retention, existing Finviant-hosted customer approval and payment links may continue within their original document terms; persist and export resulting financial/status changes. Stop new paid outbound automation when entitlement ends. At deletion, revoke hosted document, scheduling and E-Business Card links and return a professional unavailable message. Tell owners in advance that these links end with deletion. Direct payment-provider URLs and previously downloaded/emailed files are outside Finviant's complete control; do not promise to erase customer-held copies or reverse settled payments. Reconcile pending provider events before purging and retain only the narrowly required transaction evidence under a documented hold.

Before automatic deletion is enabled, provide a complete downloadable owner archive: customers and addresses; estimates, invoices and change orders with their final PDFs; jobs; approval/payment history and balances; receipts, photos and attachments; and worker/availability records. Include a manifest and counts, test large exports, and protect downloads with owner authorization and short-lived links. An export must not consume Fin requests or require a subscription. Temporary archive downloads should expire and be removed after 7 days, never extending past workspace deletion. Existing partial exports are not adequate evidence that this requirement is complete.

Delete the tenant's database records, stored objects and versions, PDFs, photos, receipts, transcripts, generated archives, cached copies and search/AI-derived records; revoke OAuth credentials, public tokens and queued jobs. Use supported storage deletion so objects do not remain billable after database rows disappear. Remove tenant memberships and delete an Auth identity only if it has no other active/retained workspace. Never purge another tenant, the operating administrator or existing exempt beta workspaces. Delete orphaned uploads separately and bound temporary files so storage usage cannot grow between cleanup runs.

Backups need a separate, verified limit: recommend ordinary backup copies age out within 30 additional days after live-data deletion, with no customer restore after purge. Confirm every selected provider's actual retention and contractual constraints before promising that maximum. Database backups do not include Supabase Storage objects, so inventory and expire file backups separately. A disaster restore must reapply a minimal deletion ledger before reopening the service to prevent deleted records returning. Restrict the ledger to non-content identifiers and policy/job evidence, expire it after all applicable backup windows and any documented legal requirement, and never log raw documents or credentials.

“All records deleted” applies to the business workspace's service data, subject to specific legal holds. Finviant's own subscription receipts/tax records and narrowly required security, fraud or dispute evidence may need separate statutory retention; retain the minimum, restrict access, set a documented end date and review active holds quarterly. Do not retain a whole former customer's workspace indefinitely as a billing exception. Owners must download their own financial/tax records before deletion. The IRS describes different retention periods by circumstance; Finviant's 60-day service window is not a substitute for the owner's recordkeeping duties. The FTC recommends a written policy covering what is kept, why, how long and secure disposal. Review the final customer terms/privacy notice before rollout and apply the new policy to existing public users only after clear prospective notice. Do not retroactively expire the private-beta grants.

### Backend changes and acceptance required before launch

- PLAN-01 / BILL-01: implement server-owned trial, paid Individual, paid Business, active Free, expired/read-only, pending-deletion and purged states; one-time trial/Free eligibility; fixed start/end/deletion dates; verified Stripe prices and signed subscription events; renewal/dunning/cancellation/upgrade/downgrade reconciliation. Browser tier selection must never grant paid access.
- PLAN-01 / AI-01: enforce 25/100 monthly Fin requests, the shared 3-request introductory allowance, purchased balances, successful-task accounting and all voice/email/SMS/receipt/storage/customer/worker/member quotas on every server entry point. Disable future jobs/extra seats at downgrade without discarding retained financial records. Keep cost limits compatible with the advertised usable allowance.
- EXPORT-01 / RET-01: finish complete owner exports, then build a daily idempotent cleanup worker with notice history, dry-run candidates, per-tenant authorization, entitlement/hold rechecks immediately before purge, a payment/reactivation race guard, bounded batches, retryable storage cleanup, audit counts/bytes and an administrator emergency pause. A dashboard/manual-review queue can handle exceptions; it must not become indefinite storage.
- RET-01 / OPS-01 / OPS-04: test two-tenant isolation, multi-workspace identities, paid renewal just before deletion, failed notice/export/purge, pending payment reconciliation, provider credential revocation, actual object cleanup and restore-after-purge suppression in isolated staging. Publish retention/export/deletion terms and obtain the required notices/acceptance before any live purge.
- Match landing-page pricing, initial onboarding, plan selection, Plans & Usage counters, billing, locked-feature labels and upgrade text links to the same server policy. Preserve existing administrator and private-beta exceptions. Verify full trial-to-plan and expiry-to-export-to-deletion journeys before claiming implementation complete.

### Cost and margin guardrail

The working 100-account model, at full included usage, estimates approximately $4.43/month for Individual and $12.43/month for Business, leaving about 70% and 56% account operating margins at $14.99 and $28. These are planning estimates, not guaranteed net profit. They use $0.02 per heavy Fin request, shared infrastructure allocation, included delivery/scan/transcription volumes, storage/download assumptions, a low-volume US SMS sender setup and an account reserve. Advertising, development and support labor, taxes, payment mix, heavier workloads, free/trial acquisition and higher-cost SMS registrations can change the result. Revalidate measured costs and at least 50% paid-tier operating margin under COST-01 before selling these allowances. Do not introduce an annual discount until the margin supports it.

Bounded retention reduces abandoned storage growth; it does not eliminate fixed database/hosting charges. Storage quotas, upload limits, export expiry, orphan cleanup, provider retention and actual reclaimed bytes must all be measured. No purge job or new paid plan was enabled by saving this proposal.

Policy references: [FTC retention and secure disposal](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/protecting-personal-information-guide-business), [IRS recordkeeping periods](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/how-long-should-i-keep-records), and [Supabase database backup and Storage limitations](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/backups).

See [Finviant Business Solutions](#finviant-business-solutions) for separately assessed new products, optional job operations, downloads, payroll decisions and white-label/open-source candidates. These options do not change the base plans or activate any new charge.

proposals.title: Finviant Business Solutions
proposals.body:
Finviant.com can support a Finviant Office umbrella of business software, practical downloads and free introductory tools. Keep the existing Office application as the flagship. Additional products should serve a specific buyer or a substantial new workflow, use shared components where appropriate and have their own measured costs. This assessment includes the owner's request to reuse Finviant's build, evaluate payroll/expanded jobs/recurring billing and assess white-label or open-source job-management options. All names and prices below are working proposals; no additional app, storefront, provider account, license purchase or subscription has been activated.

### Independent recommendation and commercial positioning

Prioritize advanced job operations and useful downloads. A narrowly scoped field-report app is a plausible second subscription product after demand is demonstrated. Full payroll is a poor near-term expansion for this small operation: provider agreements, payroll errors, payment timing and customer support add substantial responsibilities. Payroll preparation/export is a more manageable adjacent capability. Basic recurring invoices are common enough that they should strengthen the existing plans; they are a weak standalone paid upgrade.

These are positioning hypotheses, not proven market gaps. Bookipi advertises AI tools, a scheduler and recurring invoices. Invoice2go offers appointment scheduling; Jobber advertises job costing, progress billing and recurring work. Wave already sells US payroll at $40/month plus $6 per active employee or contractor paid; Gusto's Simple retail plan is $49/month plus $6 per person. Those retail prices are competitor benchmarks, not wholesale quotes available to Finviant. Value must come from the particular workflow, ease of use and total price a customer can justify.

Basic onboarding and self-service customer-list import should be included within plan limits when available. A standard $79 import fee is withdrawn from these recommendations. Substantial manual cleanup or historical migration can be individually quoted after inspecting scope, without making ordinary setup a paid obstacle. Preserve the complete standard estimate-to-payment Business workflow when pricing new optional capabilities.

### Reusable parts of the existing build

| Existing source / capability | Potential reuse | Work still required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| React screens, onboarding and business-aware navigation | Common branded experience for another product | Extract shared components; keep existing sign-in, recovery and public document/callback URLs stable; test mobile usability |
| Customer and address services; jobs and internal worker roster | Contacts, locations, assignments and availability in a Jobs or Reports app | Product-specific data model and authorization; a worker profile is not an employee payroll record or an authorized login |
| Document PDF service and server artifact pipeline | Branded field reports, work orders, checklists and completion packs | New templates, revision rules and scoped endpoints; current invoice/estimate PDF code is not a generic report engine |
| Photos/receipt capture, financial validation and performance reporting | Job cost records, proof-of-work reports and planning tools | New cost/time allocation logic, rounding tests, file limits and reliable exports; do not treat OCR or financial calculations as already certified for a new purpose |
| Tier usage, signed-event and subscription-management patterns | Product access and metered optional services | Complete verified checkout first; add per-product entitlements and reconciliation rather than granting access from a browser selection |

Source observations: `src/services/documentPdf.ts`, `src/services/customers.ts`, `src/services/workers.ts`, `src/services/tiers.ts`, `src/services/receiptCapture.ts`, `src/lib/financialValidation.ts`, `src/components/FinancialPerformance.tsx`, `supabase/functions/document-pdf/` and subscription/signed-event handlers. Recurring-draft behavior and limitations are described in `src/components/settings/WorkspaceReadiness.tsx`. These establish potential reuse, not production readiness, exact development savings or a certified payroll/billing engine. Existing launch gates remain open.

### Expanded services and product choices

| Option | Buyer and proposed scope | Price to test, not a live price | Assessment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Advanced Operations inside Office | Existing Business users: estimated versus actual job costs, owner-approved time entries, multi-visit jobs, milestones/progress billing and recurring service plans | Earlier $9.99/month pack was a test idea; newer Jobs assessment recommends core inclusion in Business if economics pass | See Finviant Job Management Widget for the expanded current recommendation. No charge approved; maintain existing features and shared Fin/SMS/storage limits |
| Finviant Jobs as a separate product | Businesses that need operational job control and use another invoicing system | Test $19-$29/month after defining limits and costs | Reuse the same Jobs module. Validate this instead of building a separate fork; model lost Business upgrades and provide a clear bundle/upgrade path |
| Business Downloads | Service-business owners who want a useful tool without another subscription: job pricing/margin workbook, cash-flow planner and trade-specific work/checklist pack | Start with one complete $19 kit; test a genuinely larger $29-$39 bundle | First low-maintenance experiment. Sell useful formulas, instructions and trade-specific examples, not a generic blank invoice template. Customer keeps their downloaded copy |
| Finviant Field Reports | Owner-operators or small teams producing photo-backed visit, inspection or work-completion reports for clients/property managers | Test $9.99/month with bounded storage/delivery | Stronger first separate-app candidate than a generic scheduler. Reuse photos, contacts, PDF and acknowledgment patterns, then validate the niche against general form tools |
| Property maintenance log | Small property owners: asset/service history, maintenance work orders, vendor appointments, photos and costs | Price only after a focused pilot | Later candidate. Avail already offers free maintenance and income/expense tracking; generic landlord software is not an established gap. Keep any initial scope distinct from rent collection, tenant screening or legal leasing |
| Standalone scheduler or E-Business Card app | A narrow subset of the existing Business benefits | No launch price recommended | Lower priority: free scheduling alternatives exist and selling the same capability cheaply can weaken Business upgrades |

A sensible future website navigation is Products, Downloads and Free Tools, with Office prominently featured. New product paths/subdomains are proposed only; no new URL is live from this assessment. Keep one brand and a small catalog. A download can introduce customers to Office, but purchase of a file must not silently create a recurring subscription. Initial release should contain one additional offer, with demand measured before adding more.

### Payroll, job management and recurring billing decisions

| Capability | Recommendation | What would justify extra revenue |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Full payroll: direct deposits, withholding, tax filings and pay statements | Defer. Later consider a qualified payroll partner or referral arrangement | Written wholesale/revenue-share terms and enough customer demand to cover integration and support. Gusto Embedded confirms usage-based pricing and that partners handle basic inbound support; do not assume all support transfers to the provider |
| Time and payroll preparation | Evaluate within the native Business Jobs core pilot | Approved time by job/worker, internal labor cost allocation and CSV export for an external payroll provider. Do not market it as tax-compliant payroll, make classification decisions or collect bank/SSN data for this limited scope |
| Expanded job management | Prioritize a small operational upgrade | Actual versus budgeted labor/materials, overrun alerts, repeat visits, milestones and progress invoicing. Reuse existing assignments, photos and change orders as foundations; new value is their operational depth |
| Recurring invoice drafts and straightforward setup | Retain as an existing designed Individual/Business benefit | Reliable guided setup and reusable templates support conversion/retention; the current release requires draft review and has no certified automatic dispatch of every recurring invoice |
| Automated recurring billing | Validate as part of recurring-service operations | Visit schedules, renewal dates, draft/send rules, authorized autopay, failed-payment handling and reconciliation. Ordinary recurring actions use rules, not a new Fin request on every cycle |

Distinguish Finviant's subscription billing from each customer's merchant billing. Client autopay requires the merchant's verified connection, explicit customer authorization, safe payment-method handling and correct retry/refund reconciliation. Keep the no-dedicated-customer-site direction: secure invoice/approval/booking links can support the customer actions. Test month-end dates, leap years, time zones, skipped/cancelled visits, changed prices, duplicate events, partial payments and tier expiry before advertising automation. Existing Business approvals, scheduling, managed delivery and basic reminders retain their promised scope.

### Open-source and white-label options for job management

ChatGPT connectors are tools for operating an external service; they do not by themselves grant rights to embed or resell that service in Finviant. The relevant choices here are frontend components, self-hosted software and commercial reseller/OEM contracts.

| Candidate / current primary source | Job-management fit | Cost and licensing observed | Recommendation for Finviant |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SVAR React Kanban and Gantt open-source cores | Job/task stage boards and project timelines/dependencies in the existing React app | MIT core, $0 software license fee, including commercial use. Paid PRO editions add features; free core does not include all advanced resource planning, auto-scheduling or exports | Best first technical evaluation. Style as Finviant while preserving required notices; Finviant must still build persistence, permissions, scheduling rules and financial logic. These are components, not a finished job system |
| ERPNext / Frappe projects | Complete project, task, timesheet, budget/profitability and issue system | Self-hosted ERPNext is GPL-3.0 with no software license subscription; hosting, upgrades and administration remain costs. Brand/trademark policy and copyleft conditions require review for the selected packaging | A separate managed product is more plausible than installing another ERP inside Office. Larger deployment/support burden; not the first choice for a small job upgrade |
| Kimai core and plugins | Time tracking and project labor/cost records for payroll preparation | Core is AGPL-3.0. Commercial plugins have separate terms; the official plugin license requires an extended agreement for defined SaaS use and restricts reuse across installations | Conditional later candidate. Review exact core/modification obligations and plugin SaaS rights; do not assume an ordinary plugin purchase permits white-label multi-customer service |
| SuiteDash via SU1TE | Fully branded separate CRM/projects/tasks/files/scheduling platform | $14/$34/$69 per client account/month plus the partner's own Pinnacle account, currently $99/month; usage/add-ons extra. AUTOP1LOT automated checkout/onboarding is separately advertised at $1,499/year | Genuine white-label route but a different business/platform, not a native Finviant Jobs plugin. Does not meet a no-fixed-cost, pay-only-after-your-customer-pays model; weak fit for the current $28/50% target |
| Agiled reseller | Separate branded business suite with CRM, projects, scheduling and invoicing | Published $4,000 entry fee plus membership from $299/month and company licenses from $23.20/month at that membership level. Other memberships/discounts exist; company fees remain separate | Reject for the proposed low-cost launch model under the published terms. Could be reconsidered only if a materially different written OEM quote supports the economics |

Primary pages checked 2026-11-08. Free/open-source license cost does not eliminate integration, security, hosting, maintenance or support costs. A configurable board does not enforce business status transitions: dragging a card must use authorized server actions and cannot silently mark a payment received or bypass customer approval. Keep non-drag alternatives and the existing low-friction/mobile action design.

No commercially hosted candidate above was verified to charge only after a Finviant subscriber pays, without any fixed fees. A per-company vendor generally charges for the provisioned account under its contract, whether the owner has paid Finviant or not. In a future paid-provider flow, provision a customer only after verified payment when contractually supported; confirm trial, suspension, archive, export, cancellation and minimum fees in writing. A free beta must not silently create chargeable vendor accounts. The MIT components avoid recurring license fees entirely rather than deferring them until subscription activation.

### Margins, costs and validation

The saved Office pricing proposal remains $14.99 Individual / $28 Business, with 25/100 monthly requests to Fin. Candidate products and optional packs do not change those prices now. Run deterministic calculations, recurring rules and template rendering without unnecessary AI calls; reserve Fin for an explicitly requested task. Model storage, exports and message recipients/segments across all products, not just nominal license price.

The newer Finviant Job Management Widget proposal recommends testing core inclusion in Business; the following earlier pack calculation remains a hypothetical alternative, not the current pricing recommendation. For a $9.99 Advanced Operations pack, an illustrative $2.50 incremental monthly operating cost leaves $7.49 contribution per purchaser before development/acquisition/taxes and unallocated support. At 25 purchasers this is $249.75 added monthly revenue and $187.25 contribution. A $3,000 development investment would need about 16 months to recover at that constant adoption and cost, before further maintenance/acquisition costs. These are assumptions for a decision, not measured demand or profit.

For a $19 download paid with a US domestic card at Stripe's published 2.9% + $0.30, processing is about $0.85, leaving $18.15 before all other costs. A 50% fully loaded margin requires total costs at or below $9.50, leaving about $8.65 after processing for marketing, refunds, support, delivery, allocated development and overhead. A $9.99/month standalone app similarly needs all monthly allocated costs at or below approximately $5 for a 50% margin. Other payment methods, international cards, taxes and third-party storefront services can change the model. Low delivery cost alone does not establish net profit.

SuiteDash's $14 lowest client license alone consumes half of a $28 selling price. Allocating its $99 partner account over 100 clients makes that $14.99 before processing, support or usage. Consequently the published reseller route cannot meet 50% at $28 under that allocation even before other costs. Evaluate it only for a separately priced and validated managed-service offer. Gusto retail prices must never be substituted for an embedded wholesale cost quote or a promised payroll margin.

Measure conversion, actual paid take-up, cancellations, support minutes, errors, storage/egress, delivered messages and realized per-account contribution for one product at a time. Charge for clearly new operational depth or optional services, retain complete base-plan workflows and test whether bundles increase total profit after accounting for lost Office upgrades. Keep the owner's minimum 50% margin requirement; do not describe incremental contribution as guaranteed net profit.

### Shared architecture and release sequence

1. Finish the existing Office launch/security/billing/export/retention gates. Validate the top two proposed offers with 5-10 target-business interviews and actual purchase/pilot intent. Select one defined customer workflow and budget before product development.
2. Test one complete download or the Advanced Operations pilot. Downloads need useful examples, formula tests, supported formats, version/license/update terms and reliable purchase-to-delivery. Basic contact import remains included; individually quote exceptional manual work only when it creates clear value.
3. Extract only the shared components required by the selected product. Reuse code through maintained modules rather than copying the entire Office application. Keep product-specific migrations, financial rules and queues isolated; review licenses before any redistribution. New software is not certified merely because an existing source file was reused.
4. If the Jobs or Reports offer has genuine paying demand, expose a separate entry point under the Finviant Office umbrella with common identity where appropriate, explicit per-product entitlements and a clear bundle/upgrade path. An unrelated download or active mini-app must not indefinitely retain expired Office records. Shared identities/contacts require scoped exports/deletion so active products and tenants are protected.
5. Consider payroll partnership, larger managed suites or another niche only after support capacity and written provider economics are established. Confirm API/embedding/resale rights, SSO, signed events, data portability, region/backup/retention limits and incident ownership. No provider application, outreach, purchase, production credential change or new product publication is authorized by recording this assessment.

References: [Bookipi pricing](https://bookipi.com/pricing/), [Jobber capabilities](https://www.getjobber.com/pricing/), [Wave payroll](https://www.waveapps.com/payroll), [Gusto retail benchmark](https://gusto.com/product/pricing), [Gusto Embedded partner responsibilities](https://embedded.gusto.com/partners), [Jotform pricing](https://www.jotform.com/pricing/), [Avail maintenance alternative](https://www.avail.com/pricing), [Calendly free alternative](https://calendly.com/pricing/), [Stripe standard processing](https://stripe.com/pricing), [SVAR licensing](https://svar.dev/licenses/), [SVAR license agreements](https://svar.dev/licenses/license-agreements/), [ERPNext project source](https://github.com/frappe/erpnext), [ERPNext license/trademark policy](https://erpnext.com/license-trademark), [Kimai core](https://www.kimai.org/en/), [Kimai commercial plugin terms](https://www.kimai.org/en/terms-plugins.html), [SU1TE wholesale pricing](https://su1te.com/wholesale-pricing/), [SU1TE FAQ](https://su1te.com/faq/) and [Agiled reseller terms](https://agiled.app/reseller-program).

proposals.title: Finviant Job Management Widget
proposals.body:
Implementation update — 2026-11-09: The owner authorized the practical financial/Jobs/document improvements and Square integration. Implemented scope and remaining activation, accounting, multi-visit and browser/provider acceptance boundaries are recorded in FIN-01, FIN-02, JOB-01, JOB-02, PAY-02 and INV-01 above. No new paid service or customer surcharge was activated.

### Recommendation and scope

Build a native Finviant Jobs module, surfaced through a compact Home widget and the existing Jobs workspace. Extend the existing application and backend rather than embedding a second CRM/ERP. Target owner-operators and small service crews: one place to plan work, carry it out, document it, understand its margin and prepare the correct invoice. Preserve the no-dedicated-customer-site direction; customer approval, booking and payment can continue through scoped links.

Aim to match established field-service products on explicitly tested core workflows and exceed selected competitors on simplicity, integration and value. It is not credible to promise superiority to every available product, enterprise construction suite or trade-specific system. Fleet telematics, payroll, warehouse stock, compliance certificates and advanced construction planning are separate businesses with different requirements. None of the proposed additions is implemented or certified by this assessment.

Recommend including the comprehensive owner/office Jobs core in Business, subject to measured economics, rather than requiring a separate job-management vendor subscription. The earlier $9.99 Advanced Operations pack was a price experiment, not an approved charge; this newer assessment favors including the core operational workflow in Business. A separately sold Jobs product or premium service would need its own demand and margin validation. Preserve current Free/Individual functionality, the proposed 5/25 internal-worker distinction, existing beta/admin exceptions and all current customer-document functions. Proposed $14.99/$28 public pricing and revised quotas remain proposals under PLAN-01, not a statement of live billing configuration.

### Evidence and current-build fit

Reviewed branch `ux/private-testing-20261029` at `b07e19aed7288211a5bb62cd3b44bd134ef56626`. Before this documentation update, Vercel deployment `dpl_HKvkzxr2vuLefb6MLENU1hD1JruP` was READY for that commit and aliased to finviant.com/www; the remote branch and local source matched. This verifies the release reference, not runtime correctness, physical-device acceptance or provider success. No new tenant, load test, provider send or application change was performed for this assessment.

| Existing foundation observed in source | Reuse | Additional work required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Jobs list/detail, customer/site links, five work statuses, contextual Schedule/Start/Complete actions, linked invoice and history | Retain the current low-friction workflow and deep links | Structured job numbers, templates, priority, task/visit models and saved operational views |
| Separate appointment and crew mutations, availability/time-off checks, version guards and request IDs | Use the same authorized scheduling actions | Multiple independently managed visits per parent job, crew capacity and clear pending/conflict handling |
| Internal worker profiles and Team Management | Assign real workers without granting account access | Optional restricted field access, time entries, cost rates, notifications and additional skills/equipment rules |
| Completion workflow prepares an invoice for review; estimate/deposit/final-balance foundations exist | Preserve linked documents, pricing and owner review | Explicit multi-invoice/progress allocations, change-order budget versions and retry-safe completion across visits |
| Job-linked photos, receipts/expenses and financial workbook | Reuse capture, storage, validation and existing expense sources | Labor/material cost allocation, estimated-versus-actual budgets, forecasting and cost-completeness checks |
| Recurring invoice plans and occurrences; Business automatic-visit branch | Extend current recurrence rather than creating a competing scheduler | Standalone recurring service plans, per-visit editing, exceptions, completion/billing policies and series history |
| Business refresh coordinator and existing Home schedule/Needs Attention | Refresh affected views from the same records | New task/visit/cost events and query-level rollups; preserve active edits |
| PDF/artifact pipeline, customer action links, managed delivery | Produce branded work orders and completion packs | New document templates, private/public field filtering, revisions and delivery certification |

Source references: `src/pages/JobsPage.tsx`, `src/components/JobDetailsDialog.tsx`, `src/lib/jobActions.ts`, `src/services/jobs.ts`, `src/services/schedulingWorkflow.ts`, `src/services/workers.ts`, `src/services/bookkeeping.ts`, `src/lib/dashboardFinance.ts`, `src/lib/useBusinessRefresh.ts`, and migrations `20261106222808_separate_job_appointment_and_crew.sql`, `20261108131228_team_management_workers.sql`, `20261106131110_estimate_deposit_final_balance.sql` and `20261106202916_business_pro_recurring_visits.sql`.

The current details dialog has Details, Photos & Expenses and Activity; the Activity panel mainly shows record timestamps and appointment/invoice context, not a complete operational event log. Notes/materials are primarily free text. The reviewed source did not establish structured task, child-visit, labor-time, job-budget or cost-rate models. Current recurrence is tied to invoice templates and can create a job/appointment for an occurrence; that is useful groundwork, not an independent multi-visit service-management system. Reuse its idempotency, plan gating and error handling after reviewing all later migrations.

### User experience: compact widget, complete workspace

Do not crowd the Home screen with the entire module or duplicate its weekly calendar and financial widget. Add a small Jobs summary using the same data: Today's work, Needs scheduling and Needs attention. Each opens a filtered Jobs view; a count should not duplicate or disagree with the existing Needs Attention total. Preserve the shared RefreshButton, centered Quick Links label and text upgrade links.

Within Jobs, provide List, Board and Schedule views of the same records, plus search and saved filters for customer, worker/crew, date, status and overdue tasks. Timeline is useful for multi-day work but should be optional, not the default for a one-hour service call. Keep one prominent next action. A scheduled job offers Start work; rescheduling belongs within its details. Completion offers Review invoice where appropriate. Billing states must not become misleading job-board columns that imply work is complete or payment is collected.

Organize a job into Overview, Work, Schedule & Team, Costs & Profit, and Documents & Activity. Reuse the existing detail layout and Photos & Expenses entry points; on phones use a short overview and expandable sections. Reveal fields only when relevant. Create a straightforward job with customer/site, title and scope; ask for schedule, tasks or budget only when the owner needs them. Templates can prefill work without requiring repetitive setup. Required completion items should explain why they block closing the job, allow an authorized reasoned override where appropriate, and confirm what was saved.

Provide accessible keyboard/touch alternatives to dragging, readable status labels, preserved unsaved edits, undo or a safe reversible change where feasible, visible retry/pending states and tested iPhone/Android layouts. Never display an offline action as saved to the server before acknowledgment.

### Comprehensive functional requirements

| Capability | Recommended behavior | Important boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Job record and reusable templates | Stable job number; customer and service location; scope; priority; target dates; service type; private instructions; linked approved estimate/change orders; trade-specific checklist and material templates | A job may be created directly without an estimate. Do not force every business into a construction-style project form |
| Tasks, checklists and milestones | Assignee, due date, required/optional steps, simple dependencies, blocked reason, completion evidence and reusable templates | Task progress is separate from customer approval, payment and appointment status; completing a checklist must not silently bill a customer |
| Multi-day and multi-visit work | One parent job with separately scheduled visits, crew, instructions, tasks, photos, time and completion status; roll up progress and costs | Keep rescheduled/cancelled/skipped visit history. Do not represent every visit as an unrelated customer job or complete the parent while required work remains |
| Crew dispatch and capacity | Reuse profiles, work hours/time off and conflict checks; save crews; filter by worker; optional skill/equipment tags; show unassigned work and configurable buffers | Availability of a worker is different from the owner's external calendar. A skill tag is not proof of a license/certification |
| Recurring service plans | Weekly/fortnightly/monthly/custom supported cadence; clear first/end dates; skip/reschedule; edit this visit versus future series; pause/resume; customer/site history | Separate recurrence of work from recurrence of invoices. Generate a bounded future horizon, not infinite records; support jobs without automatic recurring billing |
| Time tracking and labor | Start/stop job timers, manual time entry, corrections with reasons, owner approval, estimated/actual hours and historical labor-cost snapshots | Store timer events, not a database write every second. This is time/cost preparation, not payroll, tax filing or bank payment |
| Materials and other direct costs | Planned versus used quantities; purchase cost versus billable price; supplier/subcontractor/equipment/travel costs; receipts and estimated remaining costs | Reuse existing expenses. Track a cost once even when its receipt, invoice and job are all linked; distinguish cost from sales price |
| Change orders and controlled scope | Keep original approved scope and each approved revision; show pending additional work, revised budget and resulting billable amount | Draft/unapproved extras do not automatically increase approved revenue or become a charge. Keep the existing customer approval evidence |
| Progress/deposit/final billing | Support selected completed visits or milestones, deposits, remaining balance, partial invoices and an explicit final invoice review | Prevent duplicate billing of quantities/milestones and subtract prior billing correctly. Customer payment must be confirmed through the existing verified process |
| Proof of work and closeout | Before/after photos, captions, completed checklist, optional customer acknowledgment, branded work-order/completion PDF and callback/warranty record | Keep access codes, private notes, labor rates and internal margin off customer documents; no dedicated customer portal is required |
| Communication and automation | Assignment/change/completion alerts in-app; optional email/SMS templates; remind about overdue tasks, failed automations and invoices needing review | Use shared plan delivery allowances. Ordinary workflow rules consume no Fin request; explicit AI assistance uses the plan's Fin allowance |
| Reports and operational control | Job budget/actual/forecast margin, unbilled completed work, overdue tasks, capacity, estimated-versus-actual hours and callbacks | Show missing cost data and calculation basis. Retain permission-controlled exports and existing cash-flow reports |
| Audit, history and recovery | Who changed scope, status, crew, appointment, time/cost, billing allocation or override, and when; recover from duplicate submissions and uncertain network results | An editable notes box and last-updated timestamp are not a full audit log. Apply the same account retention/export/deletion policy |

A simple property/equipment service history and warranty/callback linkage are worthwhile extensions for repeat-service trades. Start with lightweight assets and due dates, not a warehouse or regulated inspection system. Subcontractors can be internal assignable profiles without access; any external collaboration requires its own explicit permissions and notification policy.

### How it connects to the current workflow

1. A directly created job or an approved estimate resolves to the correct existing job once. Estimate revisions remain linked; approval does not create duplicate jobs on retry.
2. Scheduling creates or changes the appropriate visit/appointment through the current backend validation. Customer booking rechecks availability at commit. Crew assignment uses worker profiles, hours, time off and overlapping work; external-calendar failures show a degraded state rather than claiming conflict-free scheduling.
3. Work starts; tasks, photos, materials and time entries attach to that job/visit. Changes refresh Jobs, the main calendar, Home and the relevant customer snapshot through the existing business refresh mechanism without remounting editors.
4. Owner/authorized staff confirms completion after required work is resolved. Finviant prepares or locates the correct invoice for review, including previous deposits/progress allocations and approved changes. Nothing is emailed merely because a worker checks a box or a job changes stage.
5. Verified customer payment updates invoice balance, financial reporting and applicable attention items. Job completed and invoice paid remain independent facts. Refunds/credits update the financial side without rewriting the operational history.
6. Reopening, a callback or an additional visit preserves the prior invoice, completion evidence and cost history. Unpaid invoices and unresolved work must remain visible after a job is archived.

Preserve the five canonical work states unless an explicit migration of all consumers is justified: `lead` currently means Needs scheduling, then `scheduled`, `in_progress`, `completed`, `canceled`. Use separate flags/reasons for blocked/on-hold work, visit completion, approval and billing. Dragging a card must call the same authorized server command as the corresponding action; it cannot patch payment or approval fields directly.

### Profitability: build a real job-cost view

The current Financial Performance totals are income, expenses and Net Cash Flow. Those are useful and should remain intact. They do not establish the profit earned on an individual job. A professional job-cost feature should present these quantities separately:

| Measure | Definition / treatment |
| --- | --- |
| Approved contract value | Accepted estimate/direct job selling value plus approved change orders, excluding sales tax; pending proposals shown separately |
| Invoiced / collected / outstanding | Net posted invoice value after credits; cash received after refunds; open balance. Deposits and progress invoices must not be counted again in the final invoice |
| Estimated direct cost | Budgeted labor at internal cost rates, materials and other direct costs, with an approved budget version |
| Actual direct cost | Approved time multiplied by the cost rate captured for that work, plus allocated material/subcontractor/other costs; receipts and expense rows deduplicated |
| Forecast gross profit | Approved contract value minus actual direct costs and estimated remaining costs; clearly provisional |
| Completed-job gross profit and margin | Final net job revenue minus direct costs; margin is gross profit divided by net revenue. Show incomplete-cost warnings and a safe zero-revenue result |

Changing a worker's rate must not retroactively change last month's job cost. Owner labor has a cost distinct from the price charged to a customer. Costs entered through invoices/estimates must map to the appropriate job without being counted twice; split expenses need explicit allocation whose total cannot exceed the source expense. Timer costs and a separately entered payroll/labor expense cannot both be included for the same labor. Allocate payment-processing/refund fees consistently if included in direct cost. Keep cash movement separate from gross-profit calculations and never treat a payment as a new sale.

Report estimated, actual and forecast values with dates and cost-coverage indicators. Optional overhead allocation must be visibly separate; do not call contribution/gross profit net profit or tax-ready accounting. Preserve existing integer-cent financial reconciliation and make rounding/allocation rules explicit. The current finance aggregation excludes non-USD rows; do not silently combine currencies or turn read-only external accounting data into a second authoritative ledger. QuickBooks/accounting reconciliation remains separate from the proposed operational profitability view.

### Worker access is a separate product decision

Current internal worker profiles are not login accounts. The source's legacy `assigned_user_ids` fields can now reference worker-profile IDs; the worker migration explicitly changes appointment/time-off foreign keys to profiles. New tables must refer to the correct worker identity and tenant, not assume every assignment is an Auth user.

Owner/office job control can operate with the existing roster. Existing proposed limits remain owner-only Free, 5 internal profiles on Individual and 25 on Business, including the owner. Business currently distinguishes its authorized account-user limit from those profiles; the saved proposal is five authorized people including the owner. An owner can enter time or upload work evidence for an internal worker without granting that worker access.

For genuine field-service parity, recommend optional restricted worker access to assigned jobs/visits: see instructions, start/stop time, tick tasks and submit photos/notes for review. Restrict rescheduling, scope/prices, customer export, other workers' jobs, labor cost/margins, billing and account administration. Assigned contact/location access should end when the assignment/access is revoked, with rechecks on the server. Use verified revocable identities, not long-lived forwarded links as a substitute for worker authentication.

First validate the workflow with authorized users within existing seat limits. Enabling up to 25 field identities would be a new entitlement decision and security/cost commitment; it is not automatically included by having 25 profiles. This recommendation neither changes the current distinction nor adds access accounts. A full worker portal/PWA would require separate field-role acceptance and approval before implementation. Customer-facing secure links still need no dedicated customer site.

### Plugins, libraries and services

| Choice | Required? / additional software license fee | Recommendation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Existing React/TypeScript, Supabase/Postgres/Auth/Storage, Luxon and current refresh/UI services | Reuse; no new job-management vendor license | Preferred foundation. Build native domain records and authorized commands in the existing backend; infrastructure use still costs money |
| SVAR React Kanban MIT core | Optional, $0 license | Evaluate for the board, pinned to the actual MIT package. Keep license notices; test mobile, keyboard controls, styling and server-driven paging. Paid PRO includes capabilities not supplied by the core |
| SVAR React Gantt MIT core | Optional, $0 license | Add only if longer projects genuinely need timelines/dependencies. Resource planning, auto-scheduling and critical-path/baseline features are PRO, not a free finished dispatch engine |
| Existing recurrence plus optional rrule library | Optional new library; rrule publishes BSD-style redistribution conditions, no subscription | Extend existing server-owned recurrence first. If chosen, pin/review rrule and notices, use it for rule expansion only, and test time zones/month-end/exceptions; it does not handle bookings, access or invoices |
| Existing PDF/artifact and photo/receipt pipeline | Reuse; no new PDF SaaS required for the proposed core | Add branded work-order/closeout templates and compressed images. Optional OCR retains its existing provider usage and limits; manual cost entry must work |
| Existing maps/directions links | Reuse; Google Maps URLs require no API key | Open directions in the user's maps app/browser. Do not imply this supplies embedded route optimization, live travel-time calculations or fleet GPS |
| In-app notifications; existing email/SMS providers | No new notification vendor required for core | In-app event inbox first. Optional managed messages share normal quotas and still incur provider usage. No promise of unlimited SMS, guaranteed push delivery or new sender setup being free |
| Offline/PWA support | Later engineering choice, not a required paid plugin | Start with resilient online saves, then a bounded draft/time/photo outbox. Reauthorize on sync, merge/review conflicts, clear local tenant data on sign-out and avoid caching sensitive public/recovery tokens |

SVAR's published MIT Gantt license allows commercial/SaaS use. Its $749 PRO Developer tier explicitly excludes SaaS; the currently published Application SaaS tier is $1,899 perpetual with one year of updates/support. No paid tier is needed for the recommended initial component evaluation. A resource/timeline interface can also be built natively; decide from actual effort, performance and accessibility, not a promise that open-source code removes maintenance.

Do not add another complete PHP/Laravel CRM, ERP or white-label service merely to obtain a board, time sheet or Gantt chart. That introduces another authentication system, database, deployment and upgrade surface, and still requires reconciling customers, jobs, documents and billing. Buying source code is not blanket permission to rebrand or extract every module. The prior Business Solutions candidate review remains background research, not a procurement recommendation. No plugin installation, paid license or new provider is necessary just to approve this assessment.

### Required backend and safeguards

Add tenant-owned tasks/checklists, visits, service-series exceptions, time entries/approvals, budgets and cost allocations, private rate history, activity events and notification/outbox records. Reuse appointments as scheduled occurrences and existing financial/receipt records as cost sources. Decide the visit-to-appointment mapping and transition rules before migration; do not maintain two independently editable calendars or copy expenses into a competing ledger. Extend the present single-linked-invoice context for multi-invoice allocations without breaking existing jobs.

Every new record, foreign-key relation, server command, file reference and realtime subscription must enforce business/role scope. Private pay/cost data needs more than a hidden tab: separate restricted queries/tables or safe server projections. Validate time ranges, worker identity, visit/job state, amounts and plan entitlement on the server. Keep optimistic versions, unique request/event keys, atomic state changes and retry-safe queue dispatch. Authorized overrides require an actor/reason and do not bypass payment approval.

Current Jobs reads accumulate all business records before client-side filtering/pagination. Replace that path for the expanded workspace with indexed server-side search/filter/pagination and database summaries. Fetch detailed tasks/activity only for the open job. Scope realtime updates to the tenant and affected queries; batch changes and avoid one connection or poll loop per card. Use a queue/outbox with bounded retries, deduplication and visible failed-action recovery for provider work; a queued event is not proof of delivery.

Use the existing account quotas for compressed photos/files, temporary exports and managed delivery. Keep deterministic tasks, schedules, reminders, timers and margin calculations independent of Fin requests. Full owner exports must include visits/tasks/time/costs/documents before the saved retention/deletion policy can cover this module. Archive is not deletion; include orphan cleanup, file removal, backup limitations and scoped removal without harming another active product/workspace. EXPORT-01, RET-01, SEC/OPS, CAL-01, PAY-01, BILL-01 and COST-01 remain applicable and open until their actual acceptance evidence exists.

### Can it be offered without additional cost?

A native owner/office module can avoid additional software-license subscriptions and per-worker job-management vendor fees. It cannot have literally zero cost: development, testing, storage, database/realtime/compute, backups, support and optional messaging increase with use. Open-source licensing does not guarantee that the existing hosting allocation can absorb the load.

The saved planning model estimates Business full included usage at about $12.43/account/month at 100 accounts, against proposed $28 revenue. A 50% operating-margin floor permits $14 total operating cost, leaving approximately $1.57/account/month modeled headroom for extra load. This is narrow, unmeasured headroom, not an approved module budget or guaranteed profit; the model does not establish a 50% net margin after development, acquisition, support labor and taxes. Measure and allocate those costs before pricing a promise.

Keep costs low with start/stop timer events, server summaries, bounded recurring-work generation, in-app notifications, image compression, shared storage/message quotas and no routine AI call. Use email digests for many routine worker changes rather than delivering one email/SMS per task update. Managed recipient deliveries and SMS segments count across customer and internal messages. Do not silently reduce current included functionality to fund the new module or add unlimited photos/video, route APIs or AI searches.

Include the standard Jobs core in Business if measured unit economics meet the owner's minimum margin requirement. Preserve baseline job handling on lower tiers; use underlined links to explain Business-only depth. Consider separately priced advanced services only when there is demonstrated demand and measured costs. Full payroll, continuous GPS/geofencing, route optimization/traffic APIs, warehouse procurement, regulated certificates, heavy/unlimited media and unrestricted field collaboration remain outside the low-cost baseline unless separately scoped. These exclusions mean Finviant must not claim universal enterprise parity.

### Competitor benchmark and differentiating value

Jobber documents recurring/multi-visit work, dispatch, job checklists, time/expense tracking and job profitability; Housecall Pro documents job scheduling, mobile work, time tracking and recurring-job workflows. ServiceM8 offers a broad service-job workflow and currently advertises a US $29/month Starter plan with unlimited users and 50 jobs/month. Its higher-level job-costing/resource/form capabilities have their own plan conditions; do not attribute every advanced feature to Starter. These products set a genuine operational benchmark. AI, scheduling and recurring jobs are not unique in this market.

Finviant's proposed differentiator should be an understandable approved-scope-to-payment workflow, clear job margin with missing-cost warnings, simple mobile actions, professional branded documents, reusable work templates and integrated Fin assistance at a sustainable small-business price. Compare effective jobs/users/storage/messages/features, device support and reliability, not only a competitor's highest advertised price. Finviant's 25 profiles must not be compared with 25 competitor login users. The competitive claim becomes defensible only after the same scenarios are tested in Finviant and the selected peer plan.

### Development sequence and acceptance

1. Define the parent-job/visit/task model, unchanged base-plan functions, optional field-access policy, status/billing contract, calculation examples and representative job volume. Record the competitor scenarios and cost baseline. Resolve launch authentication/provider/export/security gates before exposing new promises to hundreds of users.
2. Build the owner/office core in isolated staging: tasks/templates, multi-visit scheduling, stage-aware workspace, time/material capture, cost completeness and profitability. Migrate legacy jobs without losing appointments, crew, links, notes, photos or invoices. This is a backend/financial project, not merely a widget redesign.
3. Extend recurring service exceptions, progress billing/allocations, completion packs, event history and failed-automation recovery. Reuse existing recurring plans and document/scheduling commands, with one source of truth and explicit rollback.
4. Only after the access policy is chosen, pilot restricted field users and bounded offline/PWA behavior. Certify the full module with representative tenants/roles, real devices, actual authorized provider journeys, monitoring and measured capacity/cost before public marketing.

Required scenarios include two-tenant isolation; assigned-worker versus office/finance access; concurrent reschedules and last-slot booking; retries that cannot duplicate jobs, visits, time or invoices; changed/removed crew and time off; missing external-calendar data; DST/month-end/leap-day recurrence and series changes; cancellation/skips/reopening/callbacks; required checklist overrides; historical rate changes and overlapping timers; split/duplicate receipts; sales tax, credits, refunds, deposits and progress allocations; incomplete costs; expired plans/tokens; offline retries; upload/export failures and full record/file deletion. Provider success, a passing unit test and a READY deployment prove different things and need separate evidence.

Set prospective performance budgets before the pilot: server-paged lists of approximately 25-50 rows; initial Jobs workspace usable within about 2 seconds on an agreed representative mobile/network profile; common API reads p95 below 1 second under the agreed staging workload; p75 LCP/INP/CLS targets consistent with the main app. These are proposed acceptance targets, not measured results or an SLA. Exercise high-history tenants, active crews, recurrence and uploads together under the existing bounded staging load plan, never billable providers without prior authorization. Instrument query/queue latency, failed transitions, duplicate suppression, storage/egress, message consumption and support effort. Confirm unit economics at the intended scale before deciding whether Business can absorb the module.

Track JOB-01 through JOB-04 below as optional roadmap work until selected. Do not make the current beta dependent on an unbuilt expansion. If any capability is advertised as included at public launch, promote its relevant acceptance work to a public gate. This proposal changes documentation only and records no task as implemented.

References checked 2026-11-08: [Jobber features](https://www.getjobber.com/features/), [Jobber plan/features](https://www.getjobber.com/pricing/), [Housecall Pro features](https://www.housecallpro.com/features/), [Housecall Pro recurring jobs](https://help.housecallpro.com/en/articles/2789168-create-a-recurring-job), [ServiceM8 feature overview](https://www.servicem8.com/feature-overview), [ServiceM8 US pricing](https://www.servicem8.com/us/pricing), [SVAR editions](https://svar.dev/licenses/), [SVAR Gantt SaaS license/pricing](https://svar.dev/react/gantt/pricing/), [SVAR license agreements](https://svar.dev/licenses/license-agreements/), [rrule source](https://github.com/jkbrzt/rrule), [rrule license](https://github.com/jkbrzt/rrule/blob/master/LICENCE), [Google Maps URLs](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/urls/get-started).

proposals.title: Finviant Dashboard, Jobs and Payments Plan
proposals.body:
Implementation update — 2026-11-09: The owner authorized the practical financial/Jobs/document improvements and Square integration. Implemented scope and remaining activation, accounting, multi-visit and browser/provider acceptance boundaries are recorded in FIN-01, FIN-02, JOB-01, JOB-02, PAY-02 and INV-01 above. No new paid service or customer surcharge was activated.

### Overall recommendation

Proceed only as a staged product plan: improve Financial Performance using Wave's clarity as inspiration, build the native Jobs core already specified, and certify reliable processor-based payments before choosing Tap to Pay distribution and platform-fee economics. These can make Finviant more compelling for owner-operators and small service crews. A polished dashboard or an additional payment logo alone does not establish better value than existing invoicing/field-service products.

Recommend retaining proposed Business at $28 with the owner/office job-management core if measured costs support the owner's margin floor. The latest owner proposal, assessed before implementation, is Stripe/Square-only automated collection, optional invoice/estimate price recovery up to 3%, and a 0.5% Finviant platform fee on Free only after 30 days. Recommend no additional Finviant fee on Individual/Business, a clearly defined Free activation clock and a distinction between ordinary built-in pricing and eligible credit-card surcharges. The earlier 0.25% capped Business experiment is superseded as the current candidate by this Free-only proposal; no fee or pricing change has been approved or activated. Preserve the separate 90-day Free access policy unless explicitly revised.

Assessment only, dated 2026-11-09 America/New_York. No UI, payment destinations, provider accounts, permissions, plan entitlements, fee settings, SDKs, native app or production integration was changed. Before this documentation update, finviant.com/www matched READY deployment `dpl_4tCZpyoHn9bWMAwDkCGEz7mW9rR1` at reviewed source `810a55fac125c8a7aa4f1eb2ae978881e4549e59`; the remote branch/local HEAD agreed. Release metadata is not live payment or device certification.

### Latest payment pricing revision: feedback before implementation

Support Stripe and Square as the only automated collection providers once both paths are certified. Retire new Venmo/PayPal/Cash App profile-link defaults consistently across setup, document creation, Fin actions, PDFs and customer links, while preserving history and valid already-issued documents. Continue manual recording of cash/check/external receipts as bookkeeping; that is distinct from advertising an additional automated payment provider. Keep bank payments and eligible wallets within supported Stripe/Square routes. Reliable automatic invoice-paid/balance/dashboard updates remain an acceptance requirement.

The requested half-percentage-point options are 0%, 0.5%, 1%, 1.5%, 2%, 2.5% and 3%. A 2.9% example is not one of these steps: a $100 pre-tax invoice becomes $103 at 3%, or $102.90 at a separately supported 2.9%. Recommend the simple requested half-point list; if 2.9% specifically is desired, add it as an explicit preset rather than silently rounding 2.9% up to 3%. Zero is the default. These percentages are a selected price-recovery allowance, not a lookup of the exact processor fee.

| Owner choice | Recommended behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Absorb processing costs | Leave the service price unchanged; merchant pays its provider costs |
| Build into prices | Apply the selected 0-3% adjustment to eligible service prices before the estimate/invoice is issued, consistently for all payment methods. Present an agreed service price rather than mislabeling it as the customer's exact Square/Stripe charge |
| Add a credit-card surcharge | Only for an eligible credit-card payment and a verified supported merchant/location/provider route, with disclosures and a rate no higher than the permitted actual-cost/network/local cap. Do not turn it into a blanket line charge on debit, ACH or cash |

A 3% maximum alone does not make a surcharge permitted. Visa's US rule limits credit-card surcharges to the applicable merchant acceptance rate or 3%, whichever is lower; debit and prepaid cards cannot be surcharged, including debit processed as credit. Notice, disclosure and transaction-reporting requirements also apply, alongside location-specific rules.
