Do not assume a general Finviant software/platform fee may be passed to the homeowner as an additional credit-card surcharge. Keep the optional Finviant 0.5% merchant fee separate from the customer's processing-cost policy; do not automatically stack 3% plus 0.5% on the cardholder.

Square's current automatic credit-card surcharge feature is an open beta with surface restrictions: it covers specified POS applications and Square Invoices, not all website/custom API checkout surfaces, and excludes ACH/debit/tips/offline/split-tender cases. Its invoice partial-payment/schedule limitations also matter to Finviant's deposits and progress payments. Do not assume this capability extends to Finviant merely because a merchant uses Square. Stripe needs its own supported, verified path. Recommend ordinary built-in pricing first; keep a separate customer credit-card surcharge disabled until the merchant/provider/location and document/reconciliation flow are certified. If the verified permitted rate is between half-point options, offer only a permissible lower step or an exact permitted preset; never round up past the cap.

A percentage adjustment is not guaranteed full fee recovery. At the illustrative Stripe domestic rate of 2.9% + $0.30, charging $103 on a $100 job incurs about $3.29 in processing, leaving $99.71 before any separate Finviant fee. Flat charges and processing of the increased total prevent a universal 3% promise. Do not automatically gross up beyond the advertised/allowed adjustment cap or claim that 2.9% alone always covers Stripe.

Document setup should show the selected treatment/rate, dollar adjustment, applicable tax calculation and final customer total before sending. Save an account default plus explicit per-document choice, with separate permission and source-of-truth fields. Preserve original unit prices/discounts and the revision's adjustment; estimate-to-invoice conversion must carry the choice once, not compound it. For a credit-only fee, disclose the base total and conditional credit-payment total before approval/payment; only the eligible payment activates it. Freeze issued revisions and terms. A later change to defaults must not silently alter approved estimates, published invoices or PDFs. Define taxable bases and surcharge tax handling for supported locations before implementation.

Payment adapters must reconcile the gross customer payment, any customer surcharge, processor fee, Finviant fee and net merchant proceeds separately. Square-side surcharging and Finviant markup must not be applied twice. The existing exact-amount verification needs an explicit supported model for a valid processor-added surcharge, rather than accepting arbitrary larger amounts. A fully paid invoice clears its correct customer obligation even when merchant fees reduce the bank payout. Partial payments/refunds, deposits, changed payment method and reissued documents require consistent calculations and history.

### 1. Professional Financial Performance dashboard

Recommend this. Its purpose remains helping the business owner understand money received, recorded spending, invoices needing payment and job results, with an immediate path to the relevant record/action. Adopt Wave's hierarchy, readable interactive summaries, meaningful charts and clear date context while retaining Finviant branding/navigation. Do not copy its identity or imply that Finviant now supplies Wave's accounting engine, bank synchronization, reconciliation or full financial statements.

Current `FinancialPerformance.tsx` already has an interactive income/expense trend, metric drilldowns, date ranges, transaction search/source filters, receipt/source links, manual entries and business refresh. `dashboardFinance.ts` reconciles integer cents and excludes non-USD rows; `bookkeeping.ts` combines invoice cash activity (including verified refund outflows) with manual/job expenses and keeps QuickBooks records separate. This is useful infrastructure to refine, not replace with invented demonstration numbers.

| Recommended element | How it should work with Finviant |
| --- | --- |
| Summary cards | Money received, recorded expenses, Net Cash Flow, open invoice balance and overdue balance; clearly label period activity versus current/as-of balances |
| Trend and comparison | Consistent period filter and comparable prior-period change, readable mobile axes and direct drilldown to the underlying transactions |
| Receivables/Needs Attention | Open the existing filtered invoices/reminder action; do not introduce a second conflicting attention list or show every sent invoice as overdue |
| Expense breakdown | Categories, largest costs and uncategorized entries with receipt/job links; distinguish customer refunds from operating costs |
| Job results | Budget, actual/forecast direct cost and gross margin from the new Jobs model once verified; show incomplete-cost flags rather than fabricated profit |
| Payment status and fees | Gross customer payment, refund, processor fee, Finviant fee if selected, pending settlement and net payout as separate figures; do not subtract a bank payout from income twice |
| Data confidence | Last updated, connected/manual source, missing costs and provider failures; unavailable data must not look like a true zero balance |
| Consistent actions | Existing Add transaction/receipt/source links, shared RefreshButton, correct permissions and text upgrade links |

Keep the weekly Home schedule first and Financial Performance next, as previously directed. Use a compact Home summary opening the fuller financial view; do not fill Home with the entire workbook or a second Jobs calendar. Preserve existing Free history restrictions and lower-tier functions; offer the same professional visual quality, with unavailable advanced features explained through the established upgrade links. Do not enable extra tier features merely by redesigning their controls.

Net Cash Flow is not a bank balance or certified accounting profit. Job gross profit is not overall net profit. Show tax amounts separately where the data supports them; do not silently exclude/refactor sales tax from cash records and call the result equivalent. Net deposit values must reconcile to gross payments, refunds and explicit fees. Accrual/cash accounting switches, balance sheets, forecasts and connected bank balances require separately defined ledgers/integrations before inclusion. Preserve current timezone, partial payments, refunded invoices, permissions and QuickBooks/non-USD boundaries. Avoid automatic AI summaries on each page load; deterministic summaries need no Fin request. Motion should be modest, optional for reduced-motion users and subordinate to accurate numbers.

Costs: no Wave subscription, Wave API or new paid chart vendor is required. Existing React/SVG and backend summaries can support the design. There is implementation and QA work, plus database/hosting/monitoring use; bank feeds and full bookkeeping would be materially larger scope. Use indexed aggregate queries and bounded transaction pages rather than downloading every entry for each card. Review a real-data desktop/mobile preview before implementation and certify totals/actions after any later build.

### 2. Professional Jobs widget and full workspace

Recommend this as the strongest functional differentiator of the three. Follow the separate Finviant Job Management Widget proposal rather than building a disconnected dashboard card. A compact Home summary opens the existing Jobs workspace with List/Board/Schedule views, one next action and direct customer/document links.

The core should include job templates, structured tasks/checklists, parent jobs with independent visits, availability/crew planning, time and material capture, approved-scope revisions, recurring service exceptions, estimated/actual/forecast costs, gross margin, deposits/progress/final invoice allocation, proof-of-work PDFs and a meaningful activity history. Current jobs, appointment/crew separation, worker profiles, receipt capture, invoice preparation and recurring invoice/visit logic are foundations to extend.

Approved scope should flow to the appropriate job; scheduling should update the existing calendar; time/material costs should update the job's financial view; authorized completion should prepare the correct invoice for review; confirmed payment should update the invoice/dashboard without implying that work and payment are the same state. Do not automatically email invoices or count a payment twice because a worker completes a checklist.

Preserve internal worker profiles versus authorized account users. Five Individual/25 Business profiles including owner do not provide five/25 worker sign-ins. Existing Business account-seat limits remain separate. Field-worker time/photo/task submission would require a separately scoped restricted role, verified identity, assigned-record authorization and cost/security testing. Pilot within existing authorized seats first; no new access entitlement was approved here.

No new job-management subscription is required for a native implementation; MIT components can help with a board/timeline but supply no secure financial or scheduling backend. This has more backend/data-migration/support work than a dashboard redesign. Costs grow with records, photos, realtime sessions, notifications and export/backup retention. Reuse shared file/message allowances, compressed images, bounded recurrence and ordinary non-AI calculations. Do not promise unlimited media or full offline field operations without costing them. JOB-01..04, GROW-02 and the existing security/provider/export gates remain open.

### 3. Stripe, Square, Tap to Pay and payment choice

Recommend dependable online checkout and automatic reconciliation first. Retain Stripe and add Square only as a deliberately supported alternative/in-person route. Do not require every business to open both accounts. One primary connected processor per workspace can drive a single professional Pay invoice entry point; eligible wallets can appear inside the provider checkout. A connected merchant and a supported device are prerequisites for in-person acceptance.

Current payment setup supports external Venmo, PayPal, Stripe and Cash App links. The hosted customer-invoice checkout has Stripe account readiness checks, server-owned balance/recipient, retry keys and signed verified payment/refund events. Its code explicitly takes no Finviant application fee. Square payment collection and platform-fee fields were not established in the reviewed source. PAY-01 remains blocked on actual merchant/provider certification; the presence of Stripe code does not establish that all businesses can currently accept live payments. Mark Paid records a payment; it does not charge a card.

Tap to Pay means a customer taps a contactless card/wallet on the seller's compatible phone. It is distinct from the customer choosing Apple Pay in an online checkout. The current React/Vite web app cannot acquire Square's native phone payment capability merely by adding a JavaScript button. A mobile-web handoff is, however, a supported route.

| Square route | Fit with the present web app | Can collect a Square developer application fee? | Assessment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mobile web to Square Point of Sale app | Finviant opens Square's installed app on supported iPhone/Android; returns to Finviant, with backend verification/recovery | No, under Square's current comparison | Best initial phone-payment feasibility pilot if an app switch is acceptable and no fee is assumed on this route |
| Native companion app / supported native SDK integration | Embed Mobile Payments SDK in an iOS/Android application; requires native integration, distribution and device/provider acceptance | Yes | Consider later if payment volume justifies the build and support. Review Tap to Pay version/beta status and Apple entitlement/device/online requirements |
| Browser-controlled Square Terminal | Web app creates checkout on separately purchased paired Terminal hardware | Yes | A web-compatible fee-bearing route, but it is dedicated hardware rather than phone-only Tap to Pay |
| Square online checkout/payment links created through supported API | Browser checkout attached to the right invoice/account/balance | Yes | Useful if Square merchants need one processor for online and in-person; adds another checkout/reconciliation path to maintain |

Square's current comparison expressly distinguishes application-fee support: Mobile Payments SDK and Terminal API support it; Point of Sale API does not. Do not add fee revenue from the mobile-web handoff to the business model. The POS API also has no Square Sandbox path, so any later pilot needs a separately authorized bounded real-device/real-payment procedure. Verify provider APIs after the return rather than trusting a URL saying success. Current native Tap documentation requires compatible phones; iPhone has an Apple entitlement/account-linking requirement and no offline Tap to Pay. Review current country/SDK release conditions before committing to the product promise.

Stripe also offers Tap to Pay through native Terminal SDKs. Square is not a prerequisite for that capability. If a native app is selected later, compare one initial native provider against the actual merchant population rather than automatically building both SDKs. Continue using Finviant's own invoice/PDF and hosted Checkout where appropriate; Stripe Invoicing is a separate optional billed product, not necessary merely to collect an existing Finviant invoice payment.

### Removing Venmo/PayPal and retaining professional options

Recommend removing standalone third-party profile-link choices from NEW setup if the owner adopts a streamlined processor model after migration planning. Their limitations include manually entered balances/references and inconsistent reconciliation. Removing these links alone creates no meaningful infrastructure saving: Finviant generally is not paying the customer's external provider processing fee today.

Keep card payments, eligible Apple Pay/Google Pay through the selected processor, bank payments where supported and reliable manual cash/check/other recording. Some customers prefer PayPal/Venmo, so reduced choice can hurt conversion; assess that tradeoff while adopting the proposed two-provider setup rather than treating fewer logos as an automatic conversion improvement. Do not impose a new processor signup on the customer just to pay an invoice.

Existing issued PDFs, approved documents and old unpaid invoices must retain trustworthy saved payment details and history. A later transition must distinguish future defaults from already-issued documents, reconcile open balances and provide a deliberate new-revision/payment-link path where needed. Do not simply hide a provider from one screen while leaving invalid validation, onboarding, AI actions, old templates or documents elsewhere.

### Who receives funds and pays fees

Treat Finviant as SaaS used by independent businesses. Each business remains the business its customer is paying. Recommend direct charges to its connected Stripe account, full Stripe Dashboard/Stripe-hosted verification where suitable, Stripe billing the merchant for processor fees, and a provider-approved configuration assigning connected-account negative balance liability to Stripe. The relevant Square route similarly processes for the authenticated seller. Finviant receives only any separately authorized platform fee, not the customer's entire invoice into Finviant's ordinary bank account for later redistribution.

Stripe's published Connect model where Stripe bills connected accounts does not impose additional platform account/payout fees. Its alternative platform-managed-pricing model currently lists $2 per active account/month plus 0.25% + $0.25 per payout, in addition to processing economics. Four payouts totaling $10,000 would illustrate $28 of those Connect costs alone: $2 + $25 + $1. That is why the setup matters more than the promise of a small platform fee. Confirm actual contractual configuration rather than assuming every Connect account is priced the same. Existing account/dashboard settings must not be silently migrated.

Prefer provider-hosted verification/onboarding and visible connection/capability/remediation status. Do not store card numbers in Finviant. Signing checks, account/location binding, secure server-side token storage/refresh, deduplication, country/currency/mode checks and owner-only destination changes remain required. Finviant still needs customer support, security, fee records and safe refund operations; provider handling of merchant verification/negative balances does not remove all platform obligations. Subscription billing to Finviant is distinct from each merchant's invoice payments.

### Transaction-fee recommendation and revenue model

The current candidate is a 0.5% Finviant platform service fee for Free-plan businesses after 30 days, with no Finviant transaction fee on Individual or Business. Processor fees apply from the first payment on every plan and are separate. This creates a paid-plan incentive while protecting Business's predictable subscription value. It is a proposal for approval, not an implemented charge.

| Plan/window | Proposed Finviant fee on supported completed invoice payments |
| --- | --- |
| Business trial / first 30 days of activated Free | 0% |
| Free day 31 through the existing 90-day access term | 0.5% |
| Individual | 0% |
| Business | 0% |
| Existing private-beta/admin grants | Preserve exemptions; no new charges from this assessment |

Recommend starting the 30-day waiver at explicit Free activation, separately from the existing 15-day Business trial. Do not silently shorten or extend either trial/Free term. Display the precise fee start date and require clear merchant agreement before any charge; a Free subscription remains $0, but payment collection is not advertised as fee-free. No automatic subscription enrollment is created. The 30/90-day clocks must be server-owned and cannot reset through sign-in, plan toggles or invoice creation. Define whether outstanding invoices can still be paid during post-expiry view/export grace and apply the approved policy consistently; the 0.5% fee does not itself grant indefinite Free access.

Deduct the agreed fee from merchant proceeds through the supported processor application-fee mechanism, rather than silently adding it to the homeowner's bill or charging a separate stored card. Charge only on the actual successfully captured invoice-payment amount, using an explicit documented gross basis and integer-cent rounding. Preserve the applicable rate/waiver version when creating the payment reservation; do not retroactively change a pending payment because settlement crosses day 30 or the business upgrades. Later payments initiated on Individual/Business use 0%. Reverse/refund fees according to a disclosed consistent policy; do not treat a saved or unpaid invoice as fee revenue.

Stripe connected-account direct charges and supported Square Payments/Checkout application-fee routes can support merchant platform fees, subject to onboarding/configuration. Square's mobile-web Point of Sale handoff cannot collect them. Recommended packaging is Free online collection via supported Stripe/Square fee-capable routes, while phone Tap to Pay via Square handoff is a proposed Business benefit with no Finviant fee. This is a future entitlement recommendation for an unbuilt feature, not removal of an existing function. If Free also receives the handoff, explicitly exempt that route from the automatic 0.5% claim or approve/cost a different collection mechanism; do not promise universal fee capture through an unsupported API.

No application fee on sending estimates/invoices, approvals, expense records, manual Mark Paid/cash/check, external payments, failed/cancelled charges or a second payout of the same funds. Do not remove legitimate offline/manual bookkeeping just to force monetization. Direct funds to the merchant's processor account; keep Finviant subscription billing separate. Processor configuration, account/payout fees, refunds, reserves, tax/fee statements and support still require COST-01/PAY-03 acceptance. Do not assume the Free fee covers all nonpaying accounts or guarantees a margin.

| Processed payments in a month where the 0.5% rule applies | Finviant fee before refunds/costs |
| --- | --- |
| $100 | $0.50 |
| $1,000 | $5.00 |
| $3,000 | $15.00 |
| $5,600 | $28.00 |

At approximately $2,998 of fee-bearing volume the extra fee equals the proposed $14.99 Individual subscription; $5,600 equals proposed $28 Business. Processor charges remain additional on all plans. These are comparison thresholds, not automatic upgrades, guaranteed user savings across different payment methods or measured demand. Under the retained 90-day Free term, the fee operates only during the later part of a temporary plan, not as indefinite recurring revenue. Eligible processor revenue share remains unapproved and unquantified. Refunds/fee statements need full reconciliation: Stripe application fees require explicit refund handling; Square normally reverses them proportionately and can debit the developer bank for insufficient fee-refund funds.

### Published US processing examples and incremental costs

Rates checked 2026-11-09, illustrative standard domestic transactions; merchant agreements, plans, card country, manual entry and optional services can change them. These are primarily the SELLER's payment costs when configured as recommended, not Finviant paying a percentage of every customer's job value.

| Payment route | Published illustration |
| --- | --- |
| Square Point of Sale / Mobile Payments SDK, card present | 2.6% + $0.15 per transaction |
| Square online API card checkout | 2.9% + $0.30; Square's own invoice/link product can have a different rate, so do not apply this blindly to every Square channel |
| Stripe online domestic card | 2.9% + $0.30 |
| Stripe ACH Direct Debit | 0.8%, capped at $5 under standard pricing; settlement/failure handling differs from cards |

For a $1,000 Free-plan Stripe online domestic-card payment after the proposed waiver, the illustrative processor charge is $29.30 and Finviant fee is $5.00, leaving $965.70 before other deductions. Square online application-fee routes need their own certified rate/fee calculation; the recommended Business-only Square POS handoff has no Finviant fee. The customer's $1,000 invoice is paid by the gross confirmed payment, not only the smaller net payout. Record fees separately. A lower ACH cost can matter more to large-ticket service businesses than Tap to Pay branding; do not unnecessarily remove bank-payment support.

| Workstream | New vendor subscription required? | Costs to Finviant that remain |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dashboard redesign | No paid Wave/chart product required | Design/engineering, data reconciliation, QA and database/hosting reads |
| Native Jobs core | No job-management SaaS required; optional MIT components | New data/workflows, financial validation, migration, storage/realtime/backup/export and support |
| Stripe online certification | No extra Connect account/payout fees under the Stripe-bills-merchant model | Integration/support/monitoring; optional products and alternative liability/pricing configurations can add charges |
| Square web/POS handoff | Square POS has a free app option; merchant processing still applies | OAuth/account binding, device/return-flow testing, signed-event/API reconciliation and dual-provider support; no automatic Finviant app fee here |
| Native Tap to Pay | SDK licensing is not the primary expense | Native application/bridge, approvals, test devices, OS updates/distribution and support. Apple program generally $99/year; Google Play $25 one-time if that distribution route is chosen |
| Web-controlled Terminal | Does not require a native Finviant phone app | Hardware purchase and device lifecycle, pairing/network/support, plus software work; decide explicitly who buys hardware |
| Finviant fee monetization | Supported app-fee rails exist; no fee activated | Contract/pricing/fee ledger, refunds, reserves, reconciliation, reporting and support. Model fees collected net of reversals, not gross volume |

The saved full-use 100-account model estimates Business at $12.43/month against $28 revenue. A 50% operating-margin floor permits $14 in operating cost, leaving approximately $1.57 modeled headroom, before additional dashboard/Jobs/payment work and unallocated development/acquisition/support labor/taxes. Do not reuse that estimate as certification for this expanded product. Measure incremental DB/storage/egress/notifications, provider configuration and support at low and high adoption, with zero optional transaction income as the subscription baseline. Include fees for processing Finviant's own subscriptions separately from merchant payment costs. COST-01 remains open.

### Competitive assessment

| Current peer offer / observed baseline | Implication for the proposed Finviant offer |
| --- | --- |
| Wave Starter $0 and Pro $19/month, with accounting/cash-flow capabilities and Pro bank-transaction automation | Better-looking cash charts do not beat a real accounting ledger. Position Finviant around connected service operations and preserve integration/export options |
| Bookipi Starter $9.99 monthly / $7.60 monthly equivalent annually; advertised scheduler, AI tools and Tap to Pay in selected countries | Finviant cannot claim AI/scheduling/Tap to Pay are unique or that $28 is cheaper. Win with demonstrated job/crew/profitability depth and a simpler operational flow |
| ServiceM8 Starter US $29/month, unlimited users and 50 jobs/month | A direct operational competitor near $28. Compare job volume, actual login users, mobile functionality, messages/storage and plan-level costing features, not 25 Finviant profiles versus unlimited competitor users |
| Finviant planned $28 Business with Jobs core, controlled Fin requests, availability/customer booking, branded documents, payment updates and E-Business Card | Potentially strong for defined small service businesses after certification. The latest Free-only fee candidate preserves no added Finviant fee on Business; total effective cost and reliability must still be compared |

Do not advertise unbuilt modules, unverified live integrations or tier proposals as released benefits. A defensible positioning is a practical service-business office from approved scope through work, job margin and payment, with a clear total price. Finviant need not outperform Wave on full accounting or enterprise job systems on every feature to be the better choice for a specific customer. Measure fewer repeated entries, correct balances, time saved, mobile task completion and successful collections using the same real scenarios in the relevant peer plans.

### Recommended sequence and acceptance

1. Resolve the existing authentication/provider/security/export/operational gates applicable to the release. Certify the existing Stripe merchant/checkout/refund path and payment-state reporting before adding fee revenue assumptions.
2. Produce a real-data financial dashboard preview and define every metric/date/source. Preserve Home order, current actions, tier limits and branding; obtain design selection separately before implementation.
3. Implement the selected owner/office Jobs core in stages using JOB-01..04, with accurate cost/time/scope/billing models and full financial/export reconciliation.
4. Test Square's web handoff and, if needed, Square online checkout in isolated supported environments. Verify actual compatible devices, correct merchant identity, cancellation/app-not-installed/return loss, pending states, retries, refunds and an online-versus-in-person race against the same invoice. No automatic completion from a browser callback; no promised application fee on the handoff.
5. Validate measured economics and customer willingness to pay. Decide the latest Free-only 0.5%/30-day candidate and cost-recovery/surcharge modes before implementation. Only then consider native Tap to Pay or Terminal hardware if adoption/revenue justify their continuing costs. Native iPhone entitlement/distribution and current SDK release/beta conditions are genuine gates, not a styling exercise.

A future build must test cross-tenant/role isolation, protected merchant-destination changes, provider token renewal/revocation, replay/signature/idempotency handling, repeated or out-of-order events, gross/fee/net reconciliation, deposits/partial/overpayments, disputes/refunds/fee-cap races, issued-document migration, supported phones/accessibility, provider outage recovery and meaningful monitoring. Existing test/live separation and admin/beta exceptions must survive. FIN-01, FIN-02, PAY-02 and PAY-03 are optional assessment roadmap items; TAP-01 remains deferred pending a separately selected scope. Nothing in this document authorizes live charges, SDK installation, payment-option removal or fee collection.

Primary surcharge references checked 2026-11-09: [Visa US surcharge requirements](https://usa.visa.com/dam/VCOM/global/support-legal/documents/merchant-surcharging-qa-for-web.pdf), [Mastercard surcharge rules](https://www.mastercard.com/us/en/business/support/merchant-surcharge-rules.html), [Square credit-card surcharges and channel restrictions](https://squareup.com/help/us/en/article/8596-set-up-and-manage-card-surcharges). Other primary references checked 2026-11-09: [Wave dashboard](https://support.waveapps.com/hc/en-us/articles/48497863638548-Overview-of-your-business-Dashboard-new-Dashboard-experience), [Wave pricing](https://www.waveapps.com/pricing), [Bookipi pricing](https://bookipi.com/pricing/), [ServiceM8 US pricing](https://www.servicem8.com/us/pricing), [Square in-person integration comparison](https://developer.squareup.com/docs/in-person-payment-options), [Square mobile-web setup](https://developer.squareup.com/docs/pos-api/build-mobile-web), [Square Mobile Payments SDK](https://developer.squareup.com/docs/mobile-payments-sdk), [Square iPhone Tap to Pay](https://developer.squareup.com/docs/mobile-payments-sdk/ios/tap-to-pay), [Square application fees](https://developer.squareup.com/docs/payments-api/take-payments-and-collect-fees), [Square fee refunds](https://developer.squareup.com/docs/payments-api/collect-fees/payment-with-app-fee-refund), [Square API/SDK pricing](https://developer.squareup.com/docs/payments-pricing), [Square seller fees](https://squareup.com/help/us/en/article/5068-what-are-square-s-fees), [Stripe Connect pricing](https://stripe.com/connect/pricing), [Stripe direct-charge hosted checkout](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/direct-charges.md?platform=web&ui=stripe-hosted), [Stripe SaaS application fees](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/saas/tasks/app-fees), [Stripe refunds/disputes](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/saas/tasks/refunds-disputes), [Stripe standard pricing](https://stripe.com/pricing), [Stripe Tap to Pay](https://docs.stripe.com/terminal/payments/setup-reader/tap-to-pay), [Apple membership](https://developer.apple.com/help/account/membership/program-enrollment/), [Google Play registration](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/6112435).

proposals.title: Finviant Invoice Ninja Benchmark
proposals.body:
Implementation update — 2026-11-09: The owner authorized the practical financial/Jobs/document improvements and Square integration. Implemented scope and remaining activation, accounting, multi-visit and browser/provider acceptance boundaries are recorded in FIN-01, FIN-02, JOB-01, JOB-02, PAY-02 and INV-01 above. No new paid service or customer surcharge was activated.

### Verdict and comparison method

Invoice Ninja is a credible primary benchmark for Finviant's invoicing, estimates, expenses, projects and subscription value. The screenshot matches published hosted plan pricing. Its documented breadth is ahead of the Finviant functions established in this review, particularly recurring dispatch/autopay, time/project work, customer self-service and financial reporting. Finviant should not claim that invoice automation alone, a generic AI label or an E-Business Card makes it the better deal.

A defensible target remains small service businesses: convenient approved-scope-to-booked-work execution, crew availability, reliable document/payment updates and understandable actual job margin. Retain $14.99 Individual / $28 Business as provisional target prices if core capabilities and measured economics justify them. Do not take payment for a roadmap or slash pricing merely to match a mature vendor. The stronger financial and Jobs workspaces matter, but attractive charts and board cards cannot substitute for the underlying records and reliable calculations.

Assessment only, dated 2026-11-09 America/New_York. Reviewed Finviant source `8764f6678fd2ccff34eb40d10381125899277b6e`; local/remote branch agreed and finviant.com mapped to READY deployment `dpl_4MZpAvnJqjpf5pP2W9HrmLnmfAsm` at that commit before this documentation change. No app implementation, merchant action, competitor account creation, native-device test or live provider certification was performed. Competitor findings are published capability/price evidence, not a hands-on quality certificate. Finviant observations describe source or saved proposals and preserve the open launch gates.

### What five clients means

Invoice Ninja advertises Free with up to five clients and unlimited invoices. A client is a person/business record, not a single invoice. It can receive repeated invoices; this is not a five-invoice allowance or five new clients each month. The current reviewed public pricing and client documentation did not settle whether archiving/deleting a client releases a hosted Free slot. Do not claim five immutable lifetime clients or promise unlimited client rotation without an authoritative clarification.

Its client guide distinguishes Archive (hide from normal lists while preserving financial history) from Delete (exclude the client's activity from default reporting; restorable) and Purge (permanent removal). Do not recommend deleting customer records as a limit workaround. Finviant likewise needs truthful cap language and must retain reporting integrity when archiving.

Invoice Ninja's ongoing Free subscription and inactive-account deletion are separate: its current terms say Free accounts inactive for three months can be scheduled for irreversible deletion. Active Free usage is not advertised as expiring after 90 days. Finviant's saved one-time 90-day Free term expires based on activation, even if active; it is not equivalent to Ninja's inactivity rule.

### Fair pricing comparison

USD hosted plans, standard published monthly prices and annual charges checked 2026-11-09. Processor charges are separate. Enterprise prices must be matched by real authorized account users, not internal worker profiles.

| Scenario | Invoice Ninja published price | Finviant saved proposal | Assessment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Small ongoing Free workspace | $0 subscription; up to 5 clients | $0 subscription, 10 active customers, one 90-day term; latest candidate adds 0.5% on supported Free payments after day 30 | Finviant offers more customer capacity during the term but is a weaker ongoing Free proposition for someone with five or fewer clients |
| One authorized user | Pro $14/month or $140/year | Individual $14.99/month; $179.88 for twelve monthly payments, no approved annual discount | Finviant is $0.99/month more; annual cost difference is $39.88 against Ninja's prepaid option. A measured better workflow must justify it |
| Two authorized users | Enterprise $18/month or $180/year | Business $28/month, with up to five authorized people | Ninja is cheaper if the buyer only needs two users and does not value the extra Finviant operational scope |
| Five authorized users | Enterprise $32/month or $320/year | Business $28/month; $336 for twelve monthly payments | Finviant is $4/month cheaper on monthly billing, but Ninja annual is $16 cheaper than twelve Finviant monthly payments |

The $18 Enterprise headline is not a five-user price and does not entitle every buyer to 100 users for $18. Likewise, Finviant's 25 internal Business worker profiles are not 25 login accounts. Compare its proposed five authorized users with Ninja's five-user bracket. Ninja Pro is one user; the Enterprise starting bracket is one/two users depending on the selector wording. Confirm final checkout quantities before external marketing.

The difference between $14 and $14.99 is less important than daily task reliability, but Ninja's annual pricing is a real competitive advantage. Do not advertise a lower annual Finviant cost without an actual approved annual offer and cost model. Keep Individual as a focused owner/operator tier rather than removing it simply because a competitor has a similar price. Its baseline should compete on useful invoicing/collection functions; Business should earn its premium through operational depth.

### Invoice automation: substantial overlap

Invoice Ninja's current advanced settings explicitly describe automatic quote-to-invoice conversion on customer approval. It also documents gateway-based payments/status tracking, customer balances, deposits/partial payments and recurring invoices that can be generated, emailed and optionally automatically charged to an authorized saved payment method. Paid Pro adds automatic late-payment reminders. External Zapier/Make/n8n integrations extend the flow further. Finviant must not market basic approve-to-invoice-to-payment automation as exclusive.

The meaningful distinction to validate is service execution: an approved estimate leading to customer selection of a valid time slot, correct worker availability, the job and calendar updating together, approved work changes, completion invoice review and actual job margin. An exact native equivalent of that crew-aware customer-booking flow was not established in the reviewed Invoice Ninja pages. This is a potential Finviant strength, not proof Ninja cannot support any scheduling through its projects or integrations.

Finviant source contains approved-document and completion workflows, linked customer/jobs, availability, recurring-invoice plans with optional visits, receipt expenses, signed Stripe checkout/refund handling and reminders. Live merchant acceptance, connected calendar/provider journeys, expanded job costs and proposed public tier rules still require the existing acceptance evidence. Current recurring behavior requires review and does not establish automatic dispatch/autopay on every occurrence; these are separate controls, not the same thing as a recurring template or Finviant's own subscription billing.

### Capability comparison and practical response

| Capability | Invoice Ninja documented offer | Finviant observation / recommended response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Quote approval, conversion and online invoice payment | Native quote approval/auto-conversion, gateway payments and balance updates | Existing foundations; finish real provider and end-to-end certification before superiority claims |
| Repeat billing | Recurring generation, email and authorized automatic charging | Recurring draft/visit foundations exist; add opt-in dispatch and merchant autopay as a separately tested workflow |
| Projects/time/board | Projects, task time, Kanban and task-to-invoice; account-user assignment on Enterprise | Current stage-aware Jobs/crew/appointments are useful; structured tasks, visits, timers, budgets and accurate costs still need the JOB roadmap |
| Financial reporting | Invoice/payment/expense/P&L reports; Enterprise bank connections | Existing cash activity, expenses, chart drilldown and workbook exports; improve reporting and job costs without claiming full accounting/bank reconciliation |
| Reusable services | Product/service catalog and invoiced products | Already present: Finviant's Saved service items. Enhance discoverability/search/packages rather than rebuilding a catalog |
| Client self-service | Client portal on Free, branded options in paid tiers | Dedicated customer site is owner-deferred. Retain secure action links; customer statements can close part of the history gap without reversing that decision |
| Billing document depth | Copying, client terms/contacts, discounts, credits and expense rebilling | Prioritize selected repeated-work shortcuts; formal credits and financial adjustments need wider ledger tests |
| Customer booking/crew availability | Exact equivalent not verified in this review | Validate Finviant's crew-aware booking and service-job flow; avoid a blanket claim that Ninja has no scheduling |
| Native AI assistant | No native Fin-style account-aware assistant established in reviewed official pages | Potential distinction only if Fin's reviewed workflows save real time; integrations may provide alternatives |
| E-Business Card | No native equivalent established in reviewed official pages | Keep Finviant's company vCard as a convenient Business bonus, not the primary justification for a subscription |

Ninja's public pages conflict on the number of free invoice templates (pricing says 11; a feature page says 4). Do not base marketing on that count without clarification. Some docs cover self-hosted/all-edition behavior rather than every hosted plan; plan availability and any gateway-specific charges need confirmation before publishing a detailed sales comparison. No assertion was established here that every Ninja payment route has no platform or third-party fees.

### Is Fin valuable enough?

Fin has potential beyond voice transcription: the current protocol can look up scoped records and prepare reviewed actions such as a customer/document/job, change order, schedule change, reminder or manual payment record. It uses record references, price checks and review/execution separation. These source controls are useful; they do not prove live accuracy, speed or adoption. AI-01 remains open.

Do not assign a monetary premium simply because the interface contains AI. Fin should remove a repeated task: turn a spoken work description into a correctly priced invoice draft, find actionable overdue invoices with direct record links, or prepare a scheduling/document update for review. It must not invent prices, treat Mark Paid as charging a card, or turn a routine deterministic reminder into an AI usage charge. Preserve one completed user task per request and failure/retry safeguards; 25/100 paid monthly requests are not an unlimited virtual-office promise.

Run a small measured pilot with roughly 10-20 target owners using the same three common tasks manually and through Fin. Record completion time, major corrections, abandoned requests, repeat usage, provider latency/cost and support. A proposed go/no-go target is at least 30% median time saved on selected tasks without incorrect or unauthorized executed changes; set the precise quality criteria before the pilot. Report actual results, not an assumed saving. If ordinary templates/buttons are quicker or most outputs need rewriting, simplify Fin's scope and reduce its prominence. The core paid product must remain attractive to someone who rarely uses AI.

I did not find a verified native E-Business Card equivalent in the reviewed Ninja catalog. That does not prove absence. A business vCard can be made by many tools, so it is a small convenience/branding benefit with modest defensibility. Retain the company-only design and existing delivery quotas; do not broaden it into per-worker named cards merely to inflate feature counts.

### Financial dashboard and Jobs: what is actually necessary

Yes to a more professional financial decision dashboard and a usable Jobs workspace. No requirement to reproduce Wave's entire accounting system or build enterprise construction software just to compete.

Financial priorities: reliable recorded receipts/refunds, open/overdue amounts, an aging breakdown, expense categories, date comparisons, unbilled work, understandable job gross margin and invoice/customer drilldowns. Use one source of truth with gross payment, fees and net payout separated. Bank balance, cash flow, gross job profit and net accounting profit have different meanings. Do not label current recorded income minus expenses a complete P&L or introduce a cash/accrual switch without the supporting accounting model. Existing QuickBooks import/CSV boundaries and current cash reporting remain intact. True bank-feed reconciliation is a larger provider/financial project with additional cost and support.

Jobs priorities: tasks/checklists, independently scheduled visits and crew capacity, estimated versus actual time/materials, billable work and change orders, budget/forecast margin, completion evidence and invoice preparation. Timers and checklists alone are not premium relative to Ninja's Free project offer. Business differentiation should come from their service-specific integration: customer-approved schedule, actual available crew, field evidence, correct scope/costs and clear next actions. Keep one stage-appropriate primary action and avoid an overloaded home screen. A Kanban component supplies presentation, not these domain rules.

### Useful additions that are relatively smaller

Relative effort below assumes Finviant's existing components and server patterns, not a delivery estimate or proof that financial changes are low-risk. No new paid plugin is inherently required for these candidates.

| Candidate | Relative effort | Why / implementation boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Copy invoice/estimate into a new draft | Low-medium | Reuse lines/customer/scope, reset number/dates, approval/payment state and provider/share identifiers; owner reviews before sending. A read-only shared copy is not this feature |
| Due-date presets, optional customer payment terms and PO/reference | Low-medium | Reduce repeated entry for service/property-manager clients. Keep today's due-date default unless the owner chooses another; snapshot terms on issued documents |
| Improve existing Saved service items | Low-medium | Add search/categories/favorites and optionally multi-line service packages. Existing description/price/tax save/add/remove/export already works in source; do not add redundant catalog entry points |
| Receivables aging and saved report presets | Low-medium | Use issued invoice due dates and remaining balances; start with clearly labeled current/as-of-now buckets. Historical aging requires an actual historical ledger/snapshot policy |
| Customer statement PDF | Medium | Consolidate invoices, payments/refunds and balances in an authorized document; reuse the PDF/artifact pipeline. Define opening balance/date/currency rules and preserve a no-portal option |
| Reviewed expense-to-invoice draft | Medium | Recover billable materials/travel while retaining the original cost record; link billed amounts and prevent duplicate/over-rebilling. An expense link alone is not a customer charge |
| Basic automatic email reminders on both paid tiers | Medium extension / commercial decision | Reuse existing reminder machinery, within each plan's shared recipient quota. It should be a collection baseline comparable with Ninja Pro; reserve Business for deeper operations, not only a simple reminder |
| Formal discounts/credit notes | Medium-high | Useful invoice parity, but affects tax, approved totals, payments/refunds and reporting; never simulate with an arbitrary unsupported negative line |

Consider one tightly compressed business logo on Free, counted within its storage allowance, while retaining Finviant branding. Ninja advertises own-logo branding on Free; Finviant currently gates hosted logo uploads to activated paid plans. This is a small potential presentation improvement to evaluate, not an approved entitlement change. Likewise, customer contacts/CC, bulk sends and billing templates can be useful later, but recipient privacy/delivery counts and batch review make them more than cosmetic fields.

Do not classify bank feeds, multi-currency accounting, warehouse inventory, multi-company ledgers, customer portals, automatic tax compliance, payroll, unrestricted custom SMTP/API access or merchant autopay as quick wins. They carry distinct financial, permission, provider, abuse and maintenance requirements. No need to build all of them for the first paid release. Preserve PORTAL-01 as deferred and introduce no external vendor purchase or source-code reuse from this benchmark.

### Subscription and Free-plan recommendations

Keep $14.99 Individual as a provisional owner/operator price if reliable invoicing, reusable work, clear receivables/statements and appropriate email automation are delivered. The extra $0.99 over Ninja Pro is not an AI entitlement by itself. Put practical collection conveniences in paid Individual where economics permit; do not force a user into Business for every function already common at $14. Any expansion of current plan gates requires a later explicit decision and PLAN-01/provider validation.

Keep $28 Business as the target for a complete small service-business operation: advanced Jobs/costs, customer booking/availability, managed communication within quotas, five authorized users and 25 internal profiles. The core Jobs/profitability should not become an additional $9.99 pack on top of $28 solely to match Ninja's ordinary projects. At today's observed scope, I would not call the product better overall value than Ninja; a demonstrated integrated service workflow could justify that position for the chosen niche. No extra Finviant Business payment fee is recommended. Additional Fin requests remain optional purchases only after the saved billing/quota plan is certified.

The current Free proposal is the weakest direct comparison for a business with up to five clients: a 10-customer allowance does not automatically compensate for a 90-day deadline and a later 0.5% payment fee when a competitor advertises ongoing free access. If the owner retains this acquisition/cost strategy, describe it transparently as 90-day Starter/Free access rather than matching a forever-Free claim. If competing on permanent Free is essential, separately model a smaller active Free Lite option (for example 5 clients, one owner, strict storage/delivery, no ongoing AI and inactivity cleanup). Do not activate that alternative, remove the fee candidate or undo the 90-day decision from an assessment. Ninja's inactivity policy is useful evidence for bounded dormant-account storage, not proof of zero cost or a retention rule to copy without notice/export safeguards.

A 0.5% fee on $3,000 of supported payments after the proposed waiver is $15, which is already near the proposed Individual subscription. That can encourage conversion, but also makes Ninja Free/Pro attractive unless Finviant offers a compelling workflow. Clearly distinguish a merchant platform fee from a customer card surcharge and retain the unsupported Square POS-handoff exception. Do not depend on fee income from users who collect offline or never process a payment through Finviant.

The prior 100-account full-use model is roughly $4.43 Individual / $12.43 Business before unallocated development, acquisition, support labor and taxes. At $28, a 50% operating-margin budget is $14, leaving about $1.57 modeled headroom before new operational load. Reducing Business to $19.99 under those assumptions yields about 37.8% operating margin; $24.99 is only just over 50%, before the new work. Hence chasing a lower headline price is not responsible without a revised cost model. Do not convert the estimate into a net-profit guarantee or offer an annual discount until measured economics support it.

### Recommended order and evidence

1. Complete the existing authentication, merchant payment, provider/delivery/calendar, export/retention and monitoring requirements relevant to advertised functions. Reliable acceptance beats a longer comparison chart.
2. Deliver selected document/report shortcuts under INV-01, preserving the existing saved services, clean stage-aware actions and manual controls. Build only the highest-value repeat tasks first.
3. Develop FIN-01 and the first JOB-01/02 slice together: useful financial summaries and basic real job time/material/budget calculations rather than a superficial dashboard redesign.
4. Certify opt-in recurring dispatch and merchant autopay under REC-01 in stages; existing completion invoices remain review-first unless the owner deliberately selects an automation rule. Sending a recurring invoice, charging an authorized stored method and billing a Finviant subscription are three different operations.
5. Measure Fin under AI-02 and existing AI-01 rather than assuming it justifies a premium. Test actual signup/onboarding/mobile job-to-payment completion and customer choice at $14.99/$28 before public superiority claims.

Track competitor plan prices/seat counts and verify current capability availability again before publishing a sales comparison.
